Chapter 1

Introduction

SmartBuildOS AI Core is a Control4 driver plus a cloud AI layer for professional Control4 dealers. The driver turns Composer programming into validated requests to the SmartBuildOS cloud and turns the cloud's results back into Composer events and variables. All AI runs in the cloud; the controller holds no AI, no history beyond a small buffer, and no AI provider key.

How to read this guide. It documents what was built and verified on the AI Core branches as of 18 November 2026 (driver branch feat/ai-core; platform branch codex/ai-core at commit 2ebbd5bd2), and nothing else. Nothing in it has been released: the branches are pushed and their pull requests are open but not merged, nothing is in the Driver Store, and no migration is applied to production or to any remote database. Every name in it is copied from the driver's driver.xml, the protocol specification or the platform source. Coloured callouts say what is simulated, in development, or blocked. The Verification status page lists every one of them.

What it does

  • Asks and explains. Composer programming can ask a question (AI_ASK), request an analysis of a room or the whole system, a scene suggestion, a report or a diagnostic. The answer arrives later as the AI Response Ready event and the AI_LAST_RESPONSE variable. It can also run the household analysis (AI_RUN_HOUSEHOLD_ANALYSIS, Run Household Analysis), whose findings appear in System Studio, not on the controller.
  • Reads history instead of guessing. In the cloud, the AI may only answer historical questions from : stored Flight Recorder event ids returned by a tool in the same turn. Confirmed causes are kept apart from possible ones; unknown stays unknown.
  • Records what programming reports. AI_RECORD_EVENT lets a dealer drop a named marker into programming, because Control4 gives a driver no way to see programming run.
  • Learns, when switched on. Learning is off by default and is switched on per property in System Studio; the homeowner can pause it, exclude rooms and kinds of activity, correct, export and erase. Deterministic detectors find routines and preferences with sample-size confidence.
  • Proposes, never decides. The model only emits typed tool calls; a deterministic permission engine authorizes each one. Device actions are proposals that a person approves; they run through the existing SmartBuildOS command queue, not through this driver.
  • Reports its health. Read-only Composer properties show the Agent link, licence, provider status, telemetry and learning state.
  • Has its own touchscreen tile. A Navigator tile shows the AI Core status to anyone; the chat opens only after an owner PIN from PIN Lock and locks again after five minutes, and an owner PIN can approve one low- or medium-risk request at a time when the homeowner allows it (Chapter 8).
  • Hears from every other SmartBuildOS driver. Each driver shows an AI Core property saying whether it found AI Core; root drivers report what they are, their state, events and faults; AI Core can ask a driver a read-only question it declared, and a driver can declare an action that a person must always approve (Chapter 6).

Architecture overview

AI Core has three layers. On the controller, the AI Core driver talks only to the SmartBuildOS Agent, hub-and-spoke, using module contract v2. The Agent relays a closed list of to one fixed platform route. In the cloud, the platform authorizes, runs the AI provider, reads Flight Recorder history and keeps learning data. People see and approve things in the interfaces: System Studio for staff and the homeowner portal. Select any component to see what it does and what it connects to.

Important limitations

  • No hardware run. No physical controller has run the driver, the Flight Recorder's v2 service, or module contract v2. The bench list is in Developer Reference.
  • No live AI call. Every provider test uses mocked HTTP built from vendor documentation; no request has gone to Anthropic or OpenAI with a real key.
  • Control4 does not tell a driver who caused a change, what the value was before, or that a programming item ran. AI Core never claims any of these; such links are labelled possible.
  • The driver never controls equipment. Its only proxy is its own touchscreen tile (a uibutton), which addresses no device; actions go through the Agent's command queue after approval.
  • Persistent programming is never written. DriverWorks has no write API for programming; a change becomes a recommendation a person carries into Composer.
  • Local pub/sub is lossy by design. The Agent's durable cloud queue is the record.
  • Platform cloud results depend on a route that is not deployed. Until /api/integrations/control4/modules/rpc is deployed, the Agent gets 404 and the driver sees cloud_refused.
  • No real booking, calendar or Places call. The concierge's only working provider is a labelled SIMULATION sandbox; nothing is booked at a real restaurant. See Chapter 9.
  • Learning is off by default. A controller collects nothing for learning until System Studio switches learning on (Chapter 7).

Chapter 2

Installation

Installing AI Core means: an Agent with contract v2 that is paired, the AI Core driver added once, the configuration delivered from System Studio, and a test of the Agent link and the provider.

Prerequisites

No physical controller has run AI Core yet. Every step and every text below comes from the driver source and from simulation (unit tests and the Director emulator); the hardware validation plan in docs/ai-core/TEST-MATRIX.md says how to check on a bench. Texts are quoted exactly as the driver writes them (docs/ai-core/INSTALLATION.md).

NeedDetail

The first Agent with v2 is built from branch feat/ai-core; no released Agent carries it yet (the latest release, 20261116.035552, is protocol 1 only). With a v1 Agent AI Core registers but shows SmartBuildOS Agent update required (module contract v2) and sends no AI request.

Obtaining the C4Z

The file is smartbuildos-ai-core.c4z. No GitHub release and no store package of AI Core has been published (both are owner actions, RELEASE.md), and there is no current local build either: the only one predates the touchscreen page and driver reporting (checklist 10.8, Blocked: no packager in this worktree).

  • Local build: make build in the driver repo writes it to dist/oss/ and copies it into ~/Documents/Control4/Drivers. make build stamps <version> with the UTC time (YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS) and its formatter rewrites tracked files, so build on a clean checkout or a scratch copy. The only build recorded in the checklist is version 20261118.091052 (92,634 bytes), which predates the touchscreen page and driver reporting; no build has been made since (10.8 is Blocked).
  • Later, a release: download it from the release's assets.
  • Updates after the first install come through the Agent's updater (the SmartBuildOS store or GitHub, the Agent's Update Source), which only updates drivers already in the project; it never adds AI Core by itself, and it never downgrades (a rollback is a manual reinstall).

Use the Agent, the Flight Recorder and AI Core from the same build.

Adding the driver in Composer

The order is Agent → Flight Recorder → AI Core:

  1. Copy smartbuildos-ai-core.c4z (and smartbuildos-flight-recorder.c4z) into the Composer drivers folder (Documents/Control4/Drivers).
  2. Make sure the Agent is installed (Agents panel) and paired: its Connection Status should read connected and its pairing shown.
  3. Optional: add SmartBuildOS Flight Recorder to any room.
  4. Items → Search → SmartBuildOS AI Core → add it to a room. Its AI Core tile appears in that room's Navigator (move or hide it like any tile). One per project: a second instance is refused by the Agent's singleton rule.
  5. For the touchscreen chat and approvals, add SmartBuildOS PIN Lock too (next section).

The AI Core tile and PIN Lock

The tile has not been opened on a real touchscreen or phone yet (KNOWN-ISSUES.md KI-53 to KI-60). These steps are INSTALLATION.md §10.

  1. Check the address. Webview Address reads http://<controller>:47871/app (home network only). If it reads Controller address unknown: set App Relay Address, set App Relay Address to the controller's LAN address, and the same value on PIN Lock; then run the action Republish App URL and close and reopen the tile (Navigator does not change the address of an open page).
  2. Add PIN Lock. Install SmartBuildOS PIN Lock in the same project, licence it, and create an owner code with a PIN on PIN Lock's own page. Leave its AI Core PIN Verification property on. Only owner PINs work on the AI Core tile; staff, vendor and guest codes never do. Wrong PINs count against PIN Lock's own lockout (Clear Lockouts on PIN Lock clears it).
  3. The homeowner's two switches are in the SmartBuildOS portal and are off until the homeowner turns them on: nothing in Composer turns them on (Chapter 8). Touchscreen Detail can only lower what the homeowner allowed: Basic switches the chat off, Standard never asks for household activity, Household asks for it but the cloud answers with it only when the homeowner's switch is on.
  4. Home network only. A touchscreen or a phone on the home Wi-Fi reaches the page; a phone away from home does not (the page says so). There is no cloud fallback.
  5. Check it. Open the tile: the status shows Online and that PIN Lock is ready for this screen. Touchscreen Approvals says in plain words what is missing when it is not.

Controller selection

Add AI Core to the controller that runs the SmartBuildOS Agent: the driver finds the Agent on the same project (no smartbuildos.c4z found means no_agent), and the module registry, pub/sub and requests all run inside that Agent. Only one AI Core can be live per controller.

Connections

AI Core declares one proxy and one connection, both for its touchscreen tile: a primary uibutton proxy on binding 5001 (connection 5001, UIBUTTON), with a web view (controller://driver/smartbuildos-ai-core/app/index.html, also enabled in the phone app) — the way PIN Lock and Atmosphere build their tiles (Chapter 8). There is nothing to bind: the tile appears in the room the driver was added to. The proxy addresses no equipment. AI Core reaches the Agent with C4:SendToDevice, and the Agent reaches the cloud. Tests record every C4:SendToDevice the driver makes and show that all go to the Agent and that SetDeviceVariable, SendToProxy, SendUIRequest, RegisterDeviceEvent and Bind are never called.

Pairing with the SmartBuildOS Agent

AI Core does not pair itself: the Agent is paired (Pairing Code or the account-number flow on the Agent), and AI Core follows it. Pair the Agent before or after adding AI Core — both work: AI Core re-reads the Agent's state on every registration and on the Agent's state updates, with no reload. An Agent from this branch also registers for Director system events at the moment it is paired. At LateInit the driver sends SBOS_MODULE_REGISTER with its v2 ; the Agent answers SBOS_MODULE_REGISTERED with a per-registration token and forwards the last SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG for SBOS_AI_CORE. Registration retries every 30 s, doubling to 5 min.

Verifying communication

  1. Test Agent Link (Actions). Last Test Result should read Agent link: OK at <time> — Agent <version>, protocol 1..2, paired, cloud connected; N module(s). registered at protocol 1; this driver needs an Agent update (protocol 2) means the Agent is too old.
  2. Print Diagnostics writes the state, licence, configuration, Flight Recorder link, collection plan and every counter to the Lua output.
  3. In the Agent, Refresh Entitlements Now, then check AI Core's License Status.

Initial synchronization

  1. In System Studio open the property's Intelligence page, tab Provider & settings (Chapter 3): choose the AI provider, enter its key, and set learning, exclusions and the permission mode.
  2. Saving republishes the configuration document. The Agent forwards it with its next delivery (the Agent's Heartbeat Interval); a change to learning on/off or to the exclusions is also sent to the controller at once as a restricted operation (Chapter 4).
  3. When it arrives: AI Provider, AI Model, AI API Credential (a status such as Configured in System Studio · Anthropic ••••abcd, never a key), Permission Mode (observe, recommend or execute_low_risk + (set in System Studio)) fill in, Learning Status reads Active if learning was switched on, and Last Synchronization shows the time. Property ID and Controller ID keep reading Not delivered yet (System Studio): the platform's document does not carry them (KNOWN-ISSUES KI-6).
  4. Press Sync Now to re-register if needed, flush buffered events, re-read the directory and ask the platform's status op (body {request_id} only).
  5. Press Test AI Connection. Expected: AI connection: test accepted (job …); result follows as AI Response Ready, then the AI Response Ready event and AI_LAST_RESPONSE. Until the platform route is deployed it reads AI connection: refused (cloud_refused).

    Chapter 3

    AI Provider Setup

    AI Core uses the customer's own Anthropic (Claude) or OpenAI account. Provider setup happens in System Studio, on the property's Intelligence page, tab Provider & settings. The key is write-only: it is encrypted in the AI Core vault, never shown again and never sent to the controller. Composer only ever shows a status line such as Configured in System Studio · Anthropic ••••abcd.

    How the provider layer works

    One neutral interface sits over both vendors (src/lib/ai-core/providers/): Anthropic through the Messages API and OpenAI through the Responses API with store:false. Call sites ask for a model class, deep or fast, never a model id. Keys are passed per call and never stored by the library; it reads no environment variable for keys. toolChoice is auto or none only, and no temperature is sent.

    Provider & settings in System Studio

    System Studio → the property → Intelligence → Provider & settings. The page has two cards. Reading needs monitoring:view; saving keys and settings needs monitoring:manage (the page says Changing AI Core settings and keys needs Sentinel manage. and shows Read only for your role otherwise). The Intelligence pages appear only for a property whose controller holds the SBOS_AI_CORE entitlement.

    • Provider keys. Each stored key shows provider, ••••last4, whether it is the company key or This property's key, whether it is in use for this property, its last test result, and Test connection / Delete. Only the last four characters are ever shown. A property's own key is used before the company key. Without any key: AI Core cannot call a provider until a key is saved for this property or for the company.
    • Add or replace a key. Provider, Applies to (This property only or Every property (company key)) and the API key field, labelled Write-only. It is encrypted on arrival and never displayed or returned.
    • AI Core settings (with its revision): provider (or Use the first provider with a key), fallback provider (Used only when the provider is unreachable, never for a refusal.), model for deep reasoning and for quick answers, reasoning effort, timeout, retries, monthly spend limit (USD), daily request limit, permission mode, household learning (Learning on / Paused), excluded rooms and excluded categories.
    • Two editors. A save carries the revision it was loaded from. If someone saved in between, nothing is saved: Your changes were not saved, so nothing of theirs was overwritten. Reload to see their version, then make your change again. (HTTP 409).
    • Household analysis schedule (added after the screenshot above was taken): off by default, or daily or weekly at an hour in the property's local time, with the saved schedule's next and last runs (Chapter 7).
    • Raising the permission mode needs homecontrol:manage as well (Raising the mode needs Home control manage); a role without it can lower the mode but not raise it.
    • Excluded rooms are picked from the property's rooms as Flight Recorder has recorded them — the same list the homeowner chooses from (stored as Director room ids; a stale id is kept and marked); excluded categories offer only the closed learning-category list.
    • After a save: Saved as revision N — The controller's configuration document (mode, learning, exclusions, provider name — never a key) is published at once and is the source of truth; a learning pause, resume or exclusion change is also sent to the controller at once. The rest reaches it with its next configuration delivery. (Chapter 4.) The earlier "next check-in" wording that the driver's KNOWN-ISSUES KI-9 describes is gone, and staff categories are now a closed list (KI-4).

    Anthropic (Claude)

    • Adapter on the official SDK @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.10.0 (SDK retries off; the layer retries itself).
    • Cache breakpoints on the last tool and the system block; effort always sent explicitly; thinking blocks replayed verbatim.
    • Key shape check: 20–512 printable characters, no spaces. A key starting sk- but not sk-ant- is refused as "That looks like an OpenAI key, not an Anthropic key."

    OpenAI

    • Adapter on the official SDK openai 7.59.0, Responses API, store:false, include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"]; reasoning items replayed verbatim.
    • Key shape check: same length rule; a key starting sk-ant- is refused as "That looks like an Anthropic key, not an OpenAI key."

    Models

    The model registry (providers/registry.ts) is the single edit point. Defaults:

    ProviderClass deepClass fast
    Anthropicclaude-opus-5-5 (default effort high)claude-haiku-5-5 (default effort low)
    OpenAIgpt-6.2-astra (default effort high)gpt-6-luna (default effort low)

    A settings override (models: { deep, fast }) may name only a model of the provider in force that the registry or the versioned price table (2026-11-18) knows: claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-fable-5-2, claude-haiku-5-5, gpt-6.2-astra, gpt-6.2-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-luna. Anything else is refused with models.deep "…" is not a known Anthropic model (or OpenAI). Effort is one of low, medium, high, xhigh, max; the stored setting defaults to medium. Model ids and prices rest on the vendor documentation fetched on 18 November 2026.

    Secure key entry

    Keys are entered only in System Studio, never in Composer. The Composer property AI API Credential is read-only status. The driver never receives, stores or displays a key, and refuses a whole configuration document if any key in it is credential-shaped (api_key, token, secret, …) or a display string looks like a key (sk-…, Bearer …, long opaque blobs).

    The Studio route behind the key form is PUT /api/monitoring/ai-core/credentials with { property_id, provider, api_key, scope? } (needs monitoring:manage). The key is encrypted with the platform's secret box; every answer carries only provider, ••••last4 and test status. A key can be company-wide or a property override (scope, default property); a property's calls use its override, else the company key. DELETE removes a key; GET lists masked keys (monitoring:view).

    PUT /api/monitoring/ai-core/credentials
Content-Type: application/json

{ "property_id": "<property uuid>", "provider": "anthropic", "api_key": "<entered in Studio, never stored in a file>", "scope": "property" }

200 { "ok": true,
      "credential": { "provider": "anthropic", "scope": "property", "masked": "••••abcd", "rotated": false, "status": "untested" },
      "credentials": [ … ], "driver_config": { … } }

    Connectivity test

    POST /api/monitoring/ai-core/credentials/test with { property_id, provider } (monitoring:manage) tests the key the property's calls would use with a token-free call, GET /v1/models on either vendor. It answers ok or the error kind (auth, permission, network, …), never the vendor's message, which can echo the key. Tests are limited to 6 per minute per property (connectivity_test_limit: "Too many connection tests. Wait a minute and try again."). Whether either vendor bills GET /v1/models could not be verified from their documentation.

    In Studio the Test connection button runs this test; too many tests answer Too many connection tests just now. Wait a minute and try again. From Composer, Test AI Connection asks the platform through cloud op test_provider (at most 5 per system per hour; the 6th answers rate_limited); the job runs the same token-free test with the key in force and delivers the result later as AI Response Ready.

    Usage limits

    Spend and rate limits are enforced in the database before every provider call (blocking, not advisory). Per-property settings and their defaults:

    SettingDefaultAllowed
    requests_per_hour601–10,000

    What a person sees when a turn cannot answer

    A conversation turn or a Composer job ends in one of a fixed set of states (orchestrator/turn.ts). The text shown is fixed: it is never the vendor's message.

    Turn statusText shown
    provider_not_configuredAI Core has no AI provider key for this property. Add one in System Studio.
    budget_exceededThis property's AI limit has been reached.
    provider_errorThe AI provider could not answer right now.
    refusedThe AI provider declined to answer that request.
    round_limitI couldn't finish answering within the allowed number of steps.
    invalid_outputI couldn't produce an answer I can verify.
    unavailableAI Core could not check this property's limits. Try again.
    unsupportedA historical answer with no surviving evidence is replaced by I don't have evidence for that.

    A conversation turn is aborted after 100 s and stored as provider_error (kind aborted). Turns use at most 4 rounds by default (ceiling 8) and 4,096 output tokens.

    When the platform reports a provider error to the home it can fire the Composer event AI Provider Error (raise_event ai_provider_error), with detail in AI_LAST_EVENT_DETAIL. Quota and auth errors deliberately do not fail over to the other vendor: a customer's spend limit should stop spend, and a rejected key should surface.

    Chapter 4

    SmartBuildOS Agent Integration

    The SmartBuildOS Agent (smartbuildos.c4z) is AI Core's only peer on the controller. It authenticates AI Core, routes its messages, relays its cloud ops, forwards its configuration, licenses it and carries its events to the cloud.

    What the Agent does for AI Core

    • Registry and tokens. Registers AI Core as ai_core and issues a per-registration token minted from C4:UUID("RANDOM") when Director returns one (otherwise the v1 generator).
    • Sender stamping. Writes from_module_id / from_instance_id itself; a module's own claim is never forwarded.
    • Cloud relay. POSTs AI Core's cloud ops to /api/integrations/control4/modules/rpc with its pairing token. The platform derives tenant and property from that token only.
    • Configuration. Forwards SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG for SKU SBOS_AI_CORE; AI Core answers SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG_ACK.
    • Restricted operations. Delivers the platform's six closed operations as SBOS_MODULE_COMMAND.
    • Durable event path. Queues AI Core's envelopes and uploads them; acknowledges with SBOS_MODULE_EVENTS_ACK.
    • Licensing. Answers the licence SDK (sbos.license) for SKU SBOS_AI_CORE.

    Registration and liveness

    LateInit registers with the v2 manifest (driver sbos.ai_core; AI Core serves no capability to other modules). On SBOS_MODULE_AGENT_HELLO it re-registers (new token) and re-subscribes; on SBOS_MODULE_DIRECTORY_CHANGED it re-reads the directory 2 s later. A liveness probe (SBOS_MODULE_DISCOVER filtered to flight_recorder) runs every 5 min, and every 30 s while the Agent is not answering. A failed probe sets agent_lost and tries to re-register; the first answer flushes the buffer. The probe exists because DriverWorks gives no delivery acknowledgement.

    Connection states

    The driver derives one state; the first matching row wins. AI_STATUS holds the code (or working while jobs are pending).

    AI_STATUSConditionSmartBuildOS Connection Status
    no_agentno smartbuildos.c4z foundNo SmartBuildOS Agent in this project
    agent_update_requiredthe Agent negotiated protocol 1SmartBuildOS Agent update required (module contract v2)
    agent_lostregistered, but the liveness probe got no directory by its deadlineSmartBuildOS Agent not responding
    registeringAgent found, registration not accepted yetRegistering with the SmartBuildOS Agent
    agent_unpairedthe Agent reports paired=falseSmartBuildOS Agent not paired
    cloud_unreachablethe Agent reports connected=false, or the last cloud call ended cloud_unreachableSmartBuildOS cloud unreachable
    unlicensedlicense.enforces() (definitive denial with enforcement on)Connected (not licensed)
    readynone of the aboveConnected

    Every change of state emits one ai_core.status envelope. AGENT_CONNECTED going true → false fires Agent Disconnected; the reason is in AI_LAST_EVENT_DETAIL.

    Configuration document

    System Studio owns the configuration. Saving AI Core settings (or a homeowner's pause or exclusion change in the portal) republishes the driver's schema 1 document through driver_config for SBOS_AI_CORE; the Agent forwards it as SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG and AI Core answers SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG_ACK. The same document can arrive by the restricted operation apply_config. The platform builds it in settings/settings.ts driverConfigDocument() and refuses to publish anything its mirror of the driver's rules (settings/driver-config.ts) refuses; six golden documents are checked on both sides by the cross-repo parity test and delivered through the real Agent in the emulator.

    {
  "schema": 1,
  "learning": { "active": true },
  "exclusions": { "rooms": [12, 40], "categories": ["security"] },
  "permission_mode": "observe | recommend | execute_low_risk",
  "provider": { "name": "Anthropic", "model": "…" },
  "credential_status": "Configured in System Studio · Anthropic ••••abcd",
  "collection": {
    "system_events": true,
    "flight_recorder_topics": true,
    "agent_events": true,
    "variables": [ { "device_id": 12, "variable": "LIGHT_STATE" } ],
    "max_events_per_minute": 60
  },
  "property_id": "…",
  "controller_id": "…"
}

    That is every key the driver accepts. What the platform sends: learning.active = learning_enabled and not paused (a homeowner's pause is "off" here); exclusions.rooms as stored; exclusions.categories translated (below); permission_mode; provider (display name and deep model, omitted when none); credential_status; collection = system events, recorder topics and Agent events on, no own variables, 60 a minute. Not sent: budgets, timeouts, retries, the fallback provider, the settings revision, and property_id / controller_id — so Property ID and Controller ID keep reading Not delivered yet (System Studio) (KNOWN-ISSUES KI-6).

    Rules (aicore.config): every key optional, and what a document does not say is not switched on; unknown keys refuse the document; any credential-shaped key name anywhere refuses it; display strings are bounded (provider.name 40, provider.model 80, credential_status 96), have no control characters and are refused if they look like a key (sk-…, Bearer …, long opaque blobs); exclusions.rooms ≤ 500 ids (the platform's own bound, so every saved list arrives whole); exclusions.categories from the closed list (general, lighting, comfort, media, security, access, safety, energy, presence, system, programming, maintenance, unknown); variables ≤ 32, never a code- or credential-named variable; max_events_per_minute 1–300. One bad field refuses the whole document: the last valid one stays in force, except learning, which an invalid document turns off (Paused by configuration: vN refused), and Last Error reads Configuration vN refused: <path>: <reason> (vM kept).

    Rooms and categories on both sides

    A room is the same thing on both sides: a Director room id — the integer an envelope's and a command's room_id carries, and the one the platform compares in flight_recorder_events.room_id when it learns. The homeowner's room list is read from rooms the Flight Recorder has recorded, so a room with no recorded event yet is not offered (KI-5). Categories are translated, not shared:

    Platform learning categoryDriver category
    lightinglighting
    climate, shadescomfort (excluding either also refuses comfort markers on the controller)
    mediamedia
    occupancypresence
    device_healthsystem, maintenance
    securitysecurity, access, safety
    scenes, keypad, othernone — no driver event carries them; the cloud alone enforces these

    Defaults: the most private, the least capable

    With no configuration, for a field a valid document leaves out, and (for learning) after an invalid document:

    FieldDefaultEffect
    learning.activefalse (off)no collection at all, AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE refused, LEARNING_ACTIVE false, Learning Status Off (not switched on in System Studio). A valid document without learning leaves it off (Paused by System Studio: the configuration does not switch it on).
    collection.system_events, flight_recorder_topics, agent_eventsfalsenothing registered, subscribed or recorded
    collection.variables[]no variable listener

    provider, credential_status, property_id, controller_idnonedisplay only

    Precedence: the document wins over set_learning

    When learning is switched on or off, paused or resumed, the platform republishes the document and sends set_learning { active, reason, config_version } to the controller at once; when exclusions change it sends apply_config { config, version } with the document it just published. config_version / version are the settings_version just published. Nothing is queued when the controller has not declared modules_v1 or the document was not published with a version, and the queued command expires after 10 minutes; the document then converges the controller at its next delivery (KI-7). The cloud stops analysing at once on a pause, independently of the controller.

    The ; set_learning only previews document version config_version:

    1. config_version given and ≤ the version in force → ignored (Completed, configuration vN already decides learning). A late or repeated operation can never undo a newer document.
    2. Otherwise it applies now and is held until a document of at least config_version is applied (without config_version: until a document newer than the one in force). An older document arriving meanwhile is applied in every other respect but does not change learning.
    3. The first document of at least that version decides learning, whatever the preview said.
    4. Switching learning on is refused while the last document was refused; switching it off is always accepted.

    An apply_config carrying a version older than the one in force is Completed as superseded and changes nothing. The held state survives a restart.

    Restricted operations

    The platform can send exactly eight , carried by the existing MODULE_COMMAND queue verb. Each accepts a closed set of argument keys, validated by the platform at enqueue (src/lib/control4/commands.ts) and again by the driver (any other key → Failed). States are reported with SBOS_MODULE_COMMAND_RESULT: Accepted, Executing, then Completed / Failed. None controls equipment, runs code or forwards a command name: the last two hand a read-only query, or an action a person approved, to the driver that declared it (Chapter 6).

    OperationArgumentsEffectStaff may send it
    apply_configconfig, versionapplies the document above; an older version is supersededno (403)
    refresh_status—repaint, ai_core.status envelope, status frameyes
    deliver_resultresponse_id (required), text (≤ 4000, required; the platform sends ≤ 2048 bytes), request_id, job_id, kind (answer, analysis, report, scene_suggestion, diagnostic), pending_approvals, recommendation_count (0–9999)sets AI_LAST_RESPONSE (≤ 1024 bytes), AI_LAST_RESPONSE_ID and counts; fires AI Response Readyno (403)
    raise_eventevent (closed list), detail (≤ 512 bytes here, cut between UTF-8 characters; the platform bounds it at 240 characters), pending_approvals, recommendation_count, correlation_id (optional, 1–96 characters)sets AI_LAST_EVENT_DETAIL, AI_LAST_CORRELATION_ID (empty without one) and counts; records one ai_core.event envelope; fires the event. ai_provider_error also sets AI_LAST_ERROR to AI provider error: <detail>, cleared by the next deliver_resultno (403)
    set_learningactive, reason (≤ 120), config_version (whole number ≥ 0, optional)learning on/off at once under the precedence rule; re-plans collectionno (403)
    run_diagnosticexactly one of device_id, room_id; noteruns the local diagnosticyes
    run_driver_queryquery_ref, module_id (never ai_core), instance_id, query_id, params (≤ 6 simple values)licence BASE; asks that driver its declared read-only query; the answer goes back as cloud op driver_query_resultno (403)
    invoke_driver_actionai_action_id, module_id, instance_id, action_id, params, declaration_hashlicence AI_ACTIONS; the Agent refuses it below Remote Control Comfort; only to a driver the Agent verified; Completed only when the driver answered; the real outcome goes back as cloud op driver_action_resultno (403)

    Staff route POST /api/monitoring/control4/commands refuses deliver_result, raise_event, set_learning, apply_config, invoke_driver_action and run_driver_query with 403 (STAFF_REFUSED_MODULE_OPERATIONS): each is produced from a record the platform owns, and a hand-made copy would bypass it — an answer no job produced, an approval event for nothing, learning switched on over the homeowner's pause, a house action nobody approved.

    raise_event accepts ai_response_ready, pattern_detected, recommendation_available, automation_conflict_detected, device_failure_pattern_detected, approval_required, action_completed, action_failed, ai_provider_error. Agent Disconnected cannot be raised by the platform: only the driver knows it.

    Buffering while the Agent is away

    • Normal path: module client stage (≤ 300, frames of ≤ 100, 30 s ack, 3 tries) → the Agent's durable acknowledged queue → the cloud.
    • No Agent answering: critical envelopes (severity warning or above) go to a persisted buffer of 50 (dedup by event_id, evict least severe then oldest, every drop counted). The rest wait in memory and are lost on restart (counted when dropped). The buffer drains oldest first when the Agent answers again.
    • Telemetry Status shows either Through the Agent: N sent, N acknowledged, N dropped; buffer N, buffer drops N or No Agent answering: N critical event(s) buffered, N waiting in memory, N dropped.

    Licence behaviour

    The Agent is the licensing authority for SKU SBOS_AI_CORE (sbos.license). On the controller, commands, run_diagnostic and collection stop only when license.enforces() — a definitive denial with enforcement on. A missing feature refuses only when enforcement is on and the status is authorised (the feature list is then definitive). Grace, trial, legacy, cloud-validation-required and no-answer states fail open. Features gated on the controller: BASE (every command, run_diagnostic, Test AI Connection) and AI_LEARNING (AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE, set_learning on, learning.active). AI_ACTIONS and AI_CONCIERGE gate nothing on the controller: the platform enforces them. A refusal shows in Last Error, e.g. AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE refused: the licence does not include AI_LEARNING.

    Who is licensed. The platform licenses SBOS_AI_CORE only through an explicit entitlement row for the controller (src/lib/ai-core/licensing.ts, used by the entitlement refresh route and by every AI Core route); no subscription plan includes it until the owner decides (owner decisions 2 and 13).

    Tested end to end in the Director emulator with real HMAC signatures and a virtual clock (checklist 3.11, 10.1): activation (the Agent asks the cloud for SBOS_AI_CORE on its own and AI Core is licensed before anyone presses anything), an assertion signed for this controller (Licensed / Permanent), one signed with another controller's secret (not honoured), grace, renewal, transfer, expiry with enforcement (unlicensed, commands refused), and the cloud down for 11 days (never bricked).

    Stated gaps:

    • No driver-side transfer workflow: transferring a licence is a platform staff action; the old controller then sees NOT_ENTITLED.
    • The platform never issues CONTROLLER_MISMATCH for SBOS_AI_CORE (only for System Link); the Agent does not compare an assertion's controller_id with its own identity — binding rests on the per-controller signing secret (KI-25).
    • An assertion that fails verification is dropped and the SKU answers LEGACY, which is operational: a forged assertion does not license AI Core, but it does not stop it either (KI-24; owner decision 11).

    Chapter 5

    Flight Recorder Integration

    The SmartBuildOS Flight Recorder is the home's history. Control4 offers drivers no way to read its own History, so AI Core answers "what happened" from Flight Recorder events: cloud-side for the AI, and from the recorder's recent local ring for diagnostics on the controller.

    Why the Flight Recorder matters

    Without it, AI Core cannot see Composer device events at all (it would need the recorder's per-driver event catalogue, and duplicating it would be the double capture the architecture forbids). With it, AI Core reads device events, variable changes and programming traces through topic subscriptions and records only what the recorder does not.

    What is collected, and by whom

    ClassFlight RecorderAI Core, recorder present (v2)AI Core, recorder absent
    Composer device eventscapture.eventconsumes topic capture.not collected (documented gap)
    Variables selected in Studioobservation.change / observation.initialconsumes topic observation.own listeners for collection.variables only → ai_core.observation.variable
    Programming markers and tracesobservation.programmed, trace.*consumes observation. / trace.; AI_RECORD_EVENT → ai_core.record (recorded with learning off too)AI_RECORD_EVENT only
    Agent-classified eventsobservation.system, when selectedleft to the recorderrecorded → ai_core.observation.agent
    Director system eventsnot capturedown collector, while learning is onown collector, while learning is on

    AI Core's own system events are the documented ids only: 17 OnNetworkBindingAdded, 18 OnNetworkBindingRemoved, 19 OnNetworkBindingRegistered, 20 OnNetworkBindingUnregistered, 48 OnDeviceOnline, 49 OnDeviceOffline, 90 OnDirectorIPAddressChanged. Consumed recorder events are not re-uploaded; they already reach the cloud through the recorder. Before anything is recorded or consumed the collector applies, in order: learning off (the default) or licence halted → nothing, and the subscription, system-event registrations and variable listeners are released; excluded room; excluded category; event-id dedup (ring of 512); per-minute budget (own observations only).

    Collection is off by default. Every collection source — Director system events, the recorder's topics, Agent events and variable listeners — follows learning. Until System Studio sends a valid document with learning.active: true, AI Core collects nothing for learning; the Flight Recorder keeps recording on its own. Not gated by learning: AI_RECORD_EVENT (a dealer's marker; only the exclusions apply), every other Composer command, the local diagnostic, restricted operations, status envelopes and the Test/Sync actions.

    Flight Recorder Link shows one of: Installed: local history served; topics subscribed · Installed (no local history service; update the Flight Recorder) · Not installed: AI Core collects its minimal set itself · Unknown (needs Agent protocol 2).

    Local history (on the controller)

    The Flight Recorder advertises four request and one topic capability. Only AI Core may request them (policy table, Chapter 6). Correlation, incident analysis and period comparison are not served locally; they are cloud tools.

    CapabilityArguments (closed)Default order
    events.querylimit 1–200 (50), cursor, order, from, to, since_seq, kinds, device_id, room_id, text (≤ 64)desc
    events.timelinelimit, cursor, from, to (default last 15 min; window ≤ 31 days), kindsasc
    events.device_historydevice_id (required), limit, cursor, order, from, todesc
    events.room_activityroom_id (required), limit, cursor, order, from, todesc
    events.subscribetopic capability over capture., observation., trace.—

    Each local event carries its event_id (the envelope id the platform stores) or no_event_id (over_upload_budget: held locally but never uploaded; not_recorded: recorded before ids were kept). truncated = true says older matching entries may have existed but are no longer held. Answers are never synthesised.

    Local diagnostics

    AI_START_DIAGNOSTIC (or run_diagnostic) asks the recorder for events.device_history {device_id, limit: 25} or events.room_activity {room_id, limit: 25} (timeout 10 s, 1 retry) and records one ai_core.diagnostic envelope. Its note says local Flight Recorder history only; causes are not inferred on the controller. With nothing to attach it says why: flight_recorder_not_installed, flight_recorder_has_no_local_history_service, flight_recorder_unknown_agent_cannot_discover, or request_failed with error_code.

    History in the cloud

    For the AI, history is read from the platform's flight_recorder_events table through seven read tools (flight_recorder_search_events, flight_recorder_get_timeline, flight_recorder_get_device_history, flight_recorder_get_room_activity, flight_recorder_correlate_events, flight_recorder_analyze_incident, flight_recorder_compare_periods). Gaps (no data, retention edge, dropped events, stale Agent, clock-suspect events) are listed, never filled in. A shared correlation id is a confirmed link; same device or room within a time window is only possible. Full schemas are in Developer Reference.

    Retention

    DataDefault retention (platform)
    Events30 days from receipt
    Traces and steps90 days
    Snapshots30 days

    The detectors depend on this: seasonal patterns always answer insufficient_history (they need ≥ 365 days), and an "unused scene" needs 90 observed days of scene recording.

    Limitations

    • The local ring is short and bounded; local answers page with a cursor (pages ~20 KB, hard cap 24 KB). A cursor is refused after Clear Local History.
    • Local pub/sub is best-effort, at-most-once, bounded at 200 envelopes per subscription (drop-oldest, counted).
    • Variables whose names contain codes or credentials (USERCODE, PASSWORD, TOKEN, …) are never recorded; payloads are redacted on the controller and again on the platform.
    • Homeowner portal access to Flight Recorder tables is not granted.
    • An old (v1) recorder, or one AI Core cannot discover, is treated as present: AI Core does not duplicate its classes.

      Chapter 6

      Driver-to-Driver Integration

      DriverWorks gives drivers no sender identity, no broadcast and no delivery guarantee. Module contract v2 supplies them, hub-and-spoke through the SmartBuildOS Agent: discovery, local pub/sub, module-to-module requests, and a closed-vocabulary cloud relay. It is a strict superset of v1, so v1 modules keep working.

      The model

      Every frame is C4:SendToDevice(id, COMMAND, params) into the receiver's ExecuteCommand. Params are strings; structured data is JSON in one param. Module → Agent frames carry the v1 auth triple (module_id, instance_id, token); the Agent ignores, without answering, any frame that fails authentication. Agent → module frames carry the recipient's triple, so another driver cannot inject answers. Negotiation: both sides support PROTOCOL_MIN = 1, PROTOCOL_MAX = 2; AI Core requires 2 and reports agent_update_required against a v1-only Agent.

      Capability discovery

      SBOS_MODULE_DISCOVER (optional filter {module_id?, capability?}) is answered by SBOS_MODULE_DIRECTORY: the Agent's state (version, protocol_min, protocol_max, paired, connected) and every registered module (module_id, instance_id, driver, driver_version, protocol, status, stale, capabilities[]). Modules not heard from for 15 minutes are stale. Tokens are never included. When a module registers, unregisters or goes stale, the Agent pushes SBOS_MODULE_DIRECTORY_CHANGED 5 s after the first change of a burst. Consumers discover; they never assume.

      Registration and the capability manifest

      SBOS_MODULE_REGISTER takes an optional manifest (JSON ≤ 2 KB, ≤ 24 capabilities). A malformed manifest does not fail registration; the reply carries manifest_error (invalid_manifest, manifest_too_large, too_many_capabilities, invalid_capability). A capability a driver cannot serve locally must not be advertised.

      {
  "driver": "sbos.flight_recorder",
  "version": "20261118.120000",
  "protocol": 2,
  "capabilities": [
    { "id": "events.query", "version": 1, "kind": "request" },
    { "id": "events.subscribe", "version": 1, "kind": "topic",
      "topics": ["capture.", "observation.", "trace."] }
  ]
}

      Subscriptions

      SBOS_MODULE_SUBSCRIBE (subscription_id, topics: 1–16 ) is answered by SBOS_MODULE_SUBSCRIBED (ok, reason, granted, refused). The Agent fans out only envelopes it accepted, in SBOS_MODULE_PUBLISH frames (≤ 25 envelopes, 1 s after the first buffered one, with a dropped count). At most 8 subscriptions per instance. Subscriptions live in Agent memory and are re-sent after every registration.

      Request / response

      The requester sends SBOS_MODULE_REQUEST (request_id, idempotency_key, to, capability, args ≤ 16 KB, deadline ≤ now + 60 s). The Agent acknowledges with SBOS_MODULE_REQUEST_ACK (Routed or Refused with a code), forwards the request to the target with the stamped sender, and relays the target's SBOS_MODULE_RESPONSE (status, error_code, result ≤ 24 KB, optional cursor). Only the instance the request was routed to may answer. Retries use the same : the Agent replays a stored answer (replayed = "true") instead of routing it twice.

      Retry rules (client library): only deadline_exceeded, target_unavailable, rate_limited and cloud_unreachable are retried — at most 2 retries, after 2 s then 5 s, with the same key and a fresh request_id.

      Command authorization (policy tables)

      The Agent holds closed policy tables; the platform mirrors them in src/lib/ai-core/protocol.ts. Anything not listed is not_permitted. Changing them is a driver release.

      TableEntries
      MODULE_REQUEST_POLICYevents.query, events.timeline, events.device_history, events.room_activity: provider flight_recorder, requester ai_core
      MODULE_TOPIC_POLICYcapture., observation., trace. → subscriber ai_core
      MODULE_CLOUD_OPS.ai_coreask, analyze_room, analyze_system, learn_preference, suggest_scene, generate_report, start_diagnostic, send_notification, set_context, status, test_provider, analyze_household (the platform side of analyze_household is being built; until it lands the platform refuses it)
      MODULE_COMMANDS.ai_core (v1 table)apply_config, refresh_status, deliver_result, raise_event, set_learning, run_diagnostic

      Rate limits per module: 30 requests/min (REQUEST and DISCOVER), 20 cloud requests/min, burst 10; at most 128 routes in flight in the whole Agent.

      Adding future drivers

      1. Choose a module_id (^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,47}$) and an owned event-type prefix; reserved prefixes today: health. (guardian), test. (commissioning_inspector), mode. (home_state), bridge. (property_bridge).
      2. Use the shared client (sbos.moduleclient) with a manifest that lists only what the driver can really serve, and require_protocol = 2 if it needs v2.
      3. Add rows to MODULE_REQUEST_POLICY / MODULE_TOPIC_POLICY / MODULE_CLOUD_OPS in the Agent and in protocol.ts together; the cross-repo parity test compares them.
      4. Answer every request exactly once with a closed-vocabulary error code; page large results with a cursor.
      5. Prove each guard by breaking it once and watching a test fail, then run the Director-emulator scenario. Bench validation on hardware is still owed for everything in v2.

      Known limits: no global ordering; module identity is bound only for reserved module ids (every SmartBuildOS root driver's: the Agent asks Director which devices run that driver file and marks the registration verified, or refuses it; whether Director answers in that form on a real controller is not yet checked: blocked, no controller, checklist 12.14) — any other module_id is self-claimed and shown unverified; legacy Composer commands to the Agent (SEND_EVENT, REPORT_*, SEND_PUSH_NOTIFICATION) remain sender-unverified because programming has no token.

      Every SmartBuildOS driver reports to AI Core

      The owner decided on 18 November 2026 that every SmartBuildOS driver, present and future, can report to AI Core. Nothing here has run on a physical controller: it is built and tested with unit tests and the Director emulator through the real Agent.

      • Who reports. 51 of the 52 driver directories carry the AI Core property (AI Core itself is the exception): 20 root drivers report through the shared helper sbos.aireport (VenueFlow only while its Remote Management property is on); 30 child drivers (Bond, MQTT, System Link, UniFi and others) only look AI Core up with a small passive module and show the result; the Agent derives its own value from its module registry. A repository-wide test fails if any driver lacks it.
      • Reference drivers with hand-written reports: Atmosphere, Mode Composer (which declares activate_mode, the only declared action in the repository) and the Flight Recorder.
      • Nothing is sent when AI Core is absent, and report text is data: AI Core and the cloud strip and bound it again, and it reaches the model only as untrusted tool results, never as instructions.
      ReportWhat a driver saysLimits
      describewhat it is: name, version, file, a one-line summary, its controls, a few vocabulary words, and the read-only queries and actions it declares≤ 8 KB; sent when it changes, when AI Core appears, and at once when AI Core says it holds none (after an AI Core restart)
      stateits current facts (up to 32), such as a temperature or a mode6 a minute, latest wins
      eventsomething that happened, with a short text10 a minute; the rest dropped and counted
      diagnostica fault or warning (info, warning or fault, a code and a text)6 a minute; the rest dropped and counted

      The report hub in AI Core. AI Core receives reports from any registered driver (the sender is the one the Agent stamped), checks each against the shapes the platform accepts, keeps the latest per driver in memory (at most 48 drivers), and uploads them in batches as the cloud op driver_reports: at most 64 items and 16 KB a batch, at most 3 batches a minute, backing off to one every 10 minutes while the cloud refuses. The platform keeps up to 64 live drivers per system and 2,000 events a day per system, and keeps the driver event log 30 days (the conductor's ruling, owner decision 21). An AI Core restart loses what was waiting (KI-45). The platform handlers exist on the platform branch but nothing is deployed (KI-46).

      The AI Core property: what a dealer reads

      Every other SmartBuildOS driver shows a read-only AI Core property (default Searching…). It takes one of exactly 15 values, held in one place (src/sbos/aivalues.lua); a test fails if any driver can paint anything else. Child drivers check again on their root's traffic at most once every 10 minutes if Director's add and remove events do not reach them (KI-42).

      ValueWhenFor the dealer
      Searching…before the first registration or directory answer; after an Agent restart; AI Core found but no report answered yetNormal for a moment after a start. If it stays, check the Agent and AI Core.
      SmartBuildOS Agent not foundno smartbuildos.c4z in the projectInstall and pair the Agent.
      SmartBuildOS Agent update requiredthe Agent speaks only protocol 1, or refuses reports (an Agent older than this policy)Update the Agent to the build that ships with AI Core.
      Not registered — Agent module list fullregistration refused: 48 modules already registeredRemove drivers the project no longer uses.
      Not installedno AI Core in the project (for a child driver: Director lists no smartbuildos-ai-core.c4z)Nothing is wrong if AI Core was not sold; the driver sends nothing.
      Found — not respondingAI Core's entry is stale, or a report got no answer before its deadlineCheck the AI Core driver is running.
      Found — AI Core update required (v‹ver›)AI Core does not offer reports (version 1), or answered that the report version is unsupportedUpdate AI Core.
      Found — not licensed (v‹ver›)AI Core is not licensedLicence AI Core; nothing is kept meanwhile.
      Found — SmartBuildOS Agent not paired (v‹ver›)AI Core answered that the Agent is not pairedPair the Agent.
      Found — reporting, cloud offline (v‹ver›)AI Core accepted the report, but the Agent has no cloud connectionCheck the controller's internet connection; reports wait in AI Core within its limits.

      Found — not verified (v‹ver›)the Agent only: AI Core registered and live, but the Agent could not verify its identityDrivers then refuse to run a declared action for it; check the AI Core installation.

      Declared read-only queries and declared actions

      A driver may declare read-only queries (for example current conditions) and actions (for example Mode Composer's activate_mode). Declarations are data inside three fixed AI tools; a driver can never add, name or shape a tool.

      Asking a driver a question. In a conversation the AI may call drivers_run_query for a query the driver declared. The platform checks the parameters against the stored declaration and sends run_driver_query; AI Core passes it to that driver (10 s), and the answer comes back as driver_query_result. The tool waits up to 15 seconds and otherwise says honestly that the answer is pending.

      A driver's action, always approved by a person:

      1. The AI can only propose it with drivers_propose_action (risk medium), in a person's conversation. Nothing runs on the model's say-so, and no pre-approved rule can match it.
      2. The proposal is at least medium risk; every action of a driver that controls a lock or security equipment is high: only the homeowner can approve it, in the portal, never with a touchscreen PIN, never automatically.
      3. The homeowner approves it (in the portal, or at the touchscreen with an owner PIN for a medium action when they switched that on). The homeowner's Composer Remote Control level must be Comfort or above.
      4. The platform sends invoke_driver_action. The Agent refuses it below Comfort; AI Core sends it only to a driver the Agent verified, once, never retried, and the driver refuses it if its declaration changed since it was approved (the declaration hash).
      5. The real outcome comes back as driver_action_result: started, completed or failed. Started is never shown as completed; an action with no answer in 20 seconds is reported failed with an unknown outcome (KI-49).

      On a real controller none of this has run: Mode Composer's activate_mode running and reporting its outcome is blocked on hardware (checklist 12.18). Staff see every reporting driver on the Studio Connected drivers page.

      Configuration contract

      The protocol is unchanged by the configuration work: configuration still travels as the v1 frames SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG / SBOS_DRIVER_CONFIG_ACK and the restricted operations apply_config / set_learning over SBOS_MODULE_COMMAND. What is new is the contract on top of them: one schema-1 document built by the platform and validated by the same rules on both sides, and a precedence rule — the configuration document wins over set_learning, and a pause or resume is sent to the controller at once instead of waiting for the next delivery. Details: Configuration document and Precedence; platform side docs/ai-core/DRIVER-CONTRACT.md.

      The Agent forwards a configuration only when its settings_version or content changed since it last forwarded one: an AI Core instance added after the current document was forwarded waits for the next change, with learning off until then (KI-8).
