      Chapter 7

      Household Learning

      AI Core learns routines and preferences from deterministic detectors with sample-size confidence; the language model phrases findings, it does not invent them. Learning is off by default and is switched on per property in System Studio. The homeowner sees everything learned in the portal — what they told us, what was inferred, and suggestions awaiting their yes — and can pause, exclude, correct, export and erase.

      Switching learning on

      • Off by default. learning_enabled defaults to false on the platform, and on the controller learning.active defaults to false: Learning Status reads Off (not switched on in System Studio), LEARNING_ACTIVE is false and nothing is collected (Chapter 4).
      • Switched on in System Studio, Intelligence › Provider & settings › Learning › Learning on (needs monitoring:manage; agree it with the homeowner first). The save republishes the document and sends set_learning to the controller at once.
      • The homeowner can pause and exclude, not switch learning on (portal PATCH /api/portal/ai-core/learning refuses nothing else; a pause reaches the controller at once and the cloud stops analysing at once).
      • Learned data in Studio and the portal's learned and recommendations areas also need the AI_LEARNING licence feature; today only an explicit licence row grants it (owner decision 7). The homeowner's review, correct, pause, export and erase controls never need the licence.

      How it learns

      The analyze_property job reads stored events, applies the homeowner's controls (pause, exclusions, erase watermark) before any detector, and runs 14 pure detectors:

      DetectorEvidence threshold
      scene_override, thermostat_override≥ 10 activations, rate ≥ 40 %
      daily_routine≥ 15 of the last 30 days, 60-minute local window
      weekly_routine≥ 4 weeks, ≥ 75 % of that weekday
      unused_scene90 observed days of scene recording, 0 activations (today always insufficient_context: no scene inventory exists)
      device_failure≥ 8 offline transitions within 7 days
      frequent_room≥ 50 events, ≥ 7 days, ≥ 15 % share
      lighting_level, shade_preference, media_volume, media_source≥ 10 samples, ≥ 5 days, modal share ≥ 40 %
      favourite_scene≥ 10 activations, ≥ 5 days, ≥ 20 % share
      automation_conflict≥ 10 change-and-revert within 120 s on ≥ 3 days (labelled possible)
      seasonal≥ 365 days of history (not built in v1; answers insufficient_history)

      Thresholds marked "AI Core v1" in the source (weekly routine, frequent room, preferences, favourite scene, automation conflict, seasonal) are this phase's choice and await architect/owner review. Analysis runs on demand (POST /api/monitoring/ai-core/patterns {action:"analyze"}), idempotent per property per 10 minutes.

      Running the household analysis: the dealer's schedule and the programming command

      Decided by the owner on 18 November 2026 and built on both branches (checklist 6.7, Completed in simulation: platform unit and browser tests and the driver suite, in the conductor's final rerun; the schedule columns are applied to no database). Every trigger goes through one entry point and one gate chain (patterns/entry.ts). The analysis makes no AI provider call, so usage budgets do not gate it; one analysis runs at a time per property.

      1. The dealer's schedule (System Studio). Intelligence › Provider & settings › Household analysis schedule: Runs — Off — only when started here or by the controller (the default), Daily or Weekly; At an hour, and On a weekday for weekly, in the property's local time. The platform checks hourly (/api/cron/ai-core-analysis), so it runs within that hour. The saved schedule's status shows the next run, the last analysis and the last scheduled run (or why it was skipped); a property without a time zone cannot run a schedule, and a slot missed by more than a few hours is not made up. It runs only while learning is on and not paused, with AI_LEARNING licensed.
      2. The programming command (Composer). AI_RUN_HOUSEHOLD_ANALYSIS, described as Run Household Analysis (op analyze_household), for example after the house goes to Sleep or from a dealer-only button. It needs AI_LEARNING; at most one accepted run an hour from the controller and one request waiting at a time (a refusal, a lost connection or a timeout does not use up the hour), and SmartBuildOS keeps its own limit of one accepted run an hour per home. The normal answer is accepted (queued); the driver is never told when the run finishes and AI Response Ready does not fire: the findings appear in System Studio. Refusals name their reason (learning_not_allowed, not_licensed, already_running, rate_limited with the wait). Whether Composer lists the command as expected is unchecked in a real Composer (KI-40).

      Confidence scores

      n = sample size, T = the detector's evidence threshold, c = consistency in [0,1]
n < T          → no finding (never rounded up)
confidence     = c × n / (n + T)       0.5·c at threshold, → c as n grows
band           = low (n < 2T) · medium (n < 4T) · high (n ≥ 4T)

      The band comes from sample size alone. For a fixed consistency the score strictly increases with the sample size.

      Confidence calculator

      Formula from patterns/confidence.ts README

      Preference memory

      Memories are structured rows with full-text search (no vector store in v1), in four categories: system, explicit_preference, behavioral, operational. Each is verified or inferred and records its source: homeowner_stated, staff_entered, detector, registry, programming or model_proposed. Statuses: active, corrected, superseded, deleted, pending. The AI reads active memories with the memory_search tool (household data; needs AI_LEARNING). Staff can add a verified fact (POST /api/monitoring/ai-core/memories), never an inference and never a person.

      From Composer: AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE

      AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE (STATEMENT ≤ 300 characters, optional ROOM) sends cloud op learn_preference. The driver refuses it locally while learning is off or paused, or when the licence (enforced) lacks AI_LEARNING. The platform records the statement as a verified explicit preference with source programming (shown to the homeowner as Your home's programming states it) and answers completed at once (job_id: null): no job is tracked and AI Response Ready is not fired. It refuses with not_permitted when learning is not enabled or is paused, the feature is missing or the room is excluded; with invalid_args for a statement that names a person; and with rate_limited beyond 100 programming memories per property.

      Pending proposals from a conversation

      In a person's conversation the AI may call memory_propose to propose one memory (never in a Composer job). A proposal is stored as pending, is not used for anything, and waits for the homeowner (portal) or authorized staff (Studio › Recommendations › Pending memories) to accept or reject it; accepting makes it active and verified, rejecting deletes it to a content-free tombstone. It never describes a person, and the property's learning controls apply first.

      What my home has learned (homeowner portal)

      In the client portal, Your home assistant › What my home has learned is the homeowner's privacy centre. The area appears only when the property is licensed with AI_LEARNING. It shows, from /api/portal/ai-core/memories and /learning:

      • Your controls: Learning is on / paused with Pause learning (and resume), Rooms not to learn from, Kinds of activity not to learn from (security is never learned from today, whatever is chosen), Download my data and Erase everything learned (behind a deliberate confirmation).
      • Suggestions waiting for your yes — The assistant suggested these. They are not used for anything until you accept them. Buttons Yes, that's right / No, reject it.
      • Things you told us — Stated by you, your integrator or your home's programming — not guesses. Buttons Change it / Delete.
      • Things we inferred — Guesses from how your home was used. Each shows how confident it is and why. They describe how devices were used, never who used them. Each shows its confidence, a Why do you think this? disclosure with the evidence counts, and That's not right — correct it / Delete.

      Behavioural analysis — what the data cannot support

      • Occupancy: device interactions are not occupancy. Room findings are interaction_based unless a motion/occupancy sensor was the source.
      • Who caused a change, and the value before: not recorded; override and conflict statements say so.
      • Security, locks, access: never learned from; no enable switch exists.
      • Away / vacation recommendations: not generated in v1.
      • Rarely used scenes: answers insufficient_context — there is no scene inventory, and it needs 90 observed days.
      • Seasonal patterns: need ≥ 365 days; answer insufficient_history.
      • No time zone: time-of-day detectors answer insufficient_context rather than use UTC.
      • Markers are not learning: the learning engine never learns from AI_RECORD_EVENT markers; it reads only observation.change.
      • Identity: no finding has a person field; inferred text is scanned for person-implying words. Residual limit: a room or device label an installer named after a person ("Emma's Room") passes through as the label.

      Correcting assumptions

      Behind the portal screen, /api/portal/ai-core/memories:

      • PATCH { property_id, memory_id, action: "correct", value, statement? } — a verified replacement; the old row becomes corrected (inferred) or superseded (verified).
      • PATCH { …, action: "accept" } — accept a pending suggestion.
      • PATCH { …, action: "assign_to_me" } — links the homeowner's own stated preference to their profile (the only way a profile is ever set).
      • DELETE ?property_id=&memory_id= — content erased; a content-free key stops the same inference being re-learned.

      Staff can dismiss a recommendation (PATCH /api/monitoring/ai-core/recommendations/[id] { to: "dismissed" }); the homeowner can dismiss one shared with them, or approve one whose approver includes the homeowner (PATCH /api/portal/ai-core/recommendations). A recommendation that needs both the homeowner and the integrator (homeowner_and_integrator; no detector produces one today: each sets the homeowner or the integrator, src/lib/ai-core/recommendations/generate.ts) records each party's approval and becomes approved only when both have; either party may dismiss it; Studio and the portal show whose approval is awaited. Nothing is executed by approving a recommendation.

      Privacy settings

      • Pause and exclusions: PATCH /api/portal/ai-core/learning { property_id, paused?, excluded_room_ids?, excluded_categories? } (categories from lighting, scenes, climate, shades, media, occupancy, keypad, device_health, security, other). The change is sent to the controller at once; while paused the driver collects nothing and releases its subscriptions and listeners, and Learning Status reads Paused by System Studio: ….
      • Export: GET /api/portal/ai-core/learning?property_id=&export=1 returns every piece of AI Core learning data about the property as JSON (Download my data).
      • Erase all: DELETE /api/portal/ai-core/learning { property_id, confirm: "erase" } deletes memories, patterns and recommendations and sets a watermark so earlier events are never analysed again; the answer states what was erased, what was kept and what is never deleted. Programming hand-offs a person accepted or carried into Composer Studio are kept (their link to the erased recommendation is cleared); hand-offs nobody acted on are removed. The Flight Recorder's own history is a separate store and is not deleted; it ages out under its own retention.
      • Household gate: staff need homecontrol:view in addition to monitoring:view to read household activity.
      • Recommendations are not customer-visible by default (customer_visible false); only staff can change it.

      Chapter 8

      Intelligent Automation

      AI Core can suggest scenes, recommend HVAC and lighting changes, and propose device actions. It never decides on its own: a deterministic permission engine authorizes every tool call, a person approves every action that is not covered by a homeowner-consented rule, and approved actions run through the existing SmartBuildOS command queue.

      The principle: the model proposes, deterministic code decides

      The language model only emits typed tool calls. Each tool is declared once with a ; the engine reads the risk from the registry, never from the model. No tool accepts Lua, shell, SQL, raw device commands or free-form command names. Each property has a , set in System Studio and shown read-only in Composer: observe (default), recommend, or execute_low_risk. Raising the mode needs homecontrol:manage as well as monitoring:manage.

      Suggested scenes

      AI_SUGGEST_SCENE (ROOM, OCCASION ≤ 120) asks for a suggestion; the result is delivered with kind scene_suggestion into AI_LAST_RESPONSE. It is a suggestion only: nothing is changed. Recommendations generated from learned patterns use the kinds lighting_scene_update, hvac_schedule, entertainment_scene, automation_conflict, away_settings, predictive_assist and service_maintenance (away settings are not generated in v1). A recommendation moves new → reviewed → approved → implementing → implemented, or is dismissed / expired (after 14 days). Recommendations never execute anything; the event Recommendation Available and AI_RECOMMENDATION_COUNT tell programming one is waiting.

      The AI can propose activating an existing scene with actions_activate_scene (scene_id), a low-risk action.

      HVAC

      actions_set_thermostat proposes one setpoint: device_id, mode (heat, cool or single, naming which setpoint) and setpoint_f between 60 and 85 °F. A value outside the bounds is refused, not repaired. The thermostat_override detector looks for setpoints that are repeatedly changed after a schedule (thermostat schedules are not visible; a change marked scheduled is used, otherwise a time recurring on ≥ 15 days stands in, flagged schedule_inferred_from_recurrence).

      Lighting

      actions_set_light proposes one light level, device_id and level 0–100. The lighting_level detector learns a preferred level per device. A low verb aimed at a device the registry does not show as that verb's kind (for example SET_LIGHT on a lock, or an unknown type) is escalated to high risk.

      Permission modes

      Mode (System Studio)What the page saysEngine
      observe (default)AI Core reads and explains. It proposes nothing to the house.every non-read class is denied (observe_mode_no_actions), so no action tool is even offered
      recommendAI Core may propose actions; every one needs approval.low → approval by the requester (the homeowner for an automation or a learned basis); medium, high and external → the homeowner
      execute_low_riskOnly low-risk actions that match a pre-approved rule may run without approval. Locks, garage and security always need the homeowner.low → allowed only on a matching active rule, otherwise as recommend; medium, high and external as recommend (no rule can ever match a medium action)

      The action lifecycle

      Every action is recorded in ai_core_actions and moves through a fixed lifecycle, enforced in TypeScript (actions/lifecycle.ts) and again by a database trigger; a unit test pins the two equal.

      FromTo
      proposedpending_approval, approved (only on a matching consented rule), denied, cancelled, expired
      pending_approvalapproved, denied, cancelled, expired
      approvedqueued, denied, failed, cancelled, expired
      queuedcompleted, failed, expired, denied — only from the linked control4_commands row (the queue's acknowledgement, decline or expiry)
      completed, failed, expired, denied, cancelled— (final)
      • Who approves, and where. A low-risk action a person asked for is approved by that requester, or by staff with homecontrol:manage (POST /api/monitoring/ai-core/actions/[id]). An action with required_approver homeowner, or risk medium or high, is the homeowner's alone; Studio says Awaiting the homeowner. Lock, garage and security actions are the homeowner's alone to approve; staff cannot approve them here. The homeowner approves in the portal (POST /api/portal/ai-core/actions) and, only for low- and medium-risk proposals and only when the homeowner has switched it on, also at the AI Core touchscreen tile with one owner PIN per item (below). High-risk actions (locks, garage doors, security), external actions, programming, recommendations and settings are approved in the portal only.
      • What was seen is what runs. An approval carries args_hash, the hash of the action as the approver saw it; a mismatch answers 409 approval_mismatch (This action changed since you saw it. Reload it and decide again.).
      • Timing and limits. A proposal waits 30 minutes for approval; the queue adds its own 1 hour after enqueue. At most 10 open actions per property, 6 proposals a minute and 40 an hour (owner decision 9).
      • Outcome. completed and failed come only from the queue row (a real driver acknowledgement), never from AI Core. The platform can raise Approval Required, Action Completed and Action Failed in Composer, with the action id in AI_LAST_CORRELATION_ID.

      Locks, garage doors and security: two confirmations

      A lock, garage or security action (or any action escalated to high risk by its target class) needs two separate homeowner confirmations: first AI Core's approval in the portal, then the command queue's own Control4 approval, which collects any disarm code. AI Core never takes, answers or pre-fills that second step. The portal says so after the first approval: Locks, garage doors and security ask again: after you approve here, the request appears in Home control requests (under Approvals), where you approve it a second time — and enter your security code if it disarms the alarm. Whether two confirmations should stay is owner decision 9.

      The AI Core touchscreen page

      AI Core has its own Navigator tile, on a touchscreen and in the phone app, served by the driver from the controller on the home network (port 47871). It is built the way PIN Lock and Atmosphere build theirs. None of it has run on a real touchscreen, phone or controller: the page, the PIN flow and the platform side were tested only with unit tests and the Director emulator (the driver side with the real PIN Lock driver in the emulator). Whether the tile opens in Navigator, whether Navigator lets the page post the PIN to PIN Lock on another port, and whether Navigator tells the page it closed are not known: blocked, no controller or Navigator (checklist 11.10–11.12).

      What it needs. SmartBuildOS PIN Lock in the same project, licensed, with an owner code (Chapter 2), and a touchscreen or phone on the home network: away from home the page cannot be reached and there is no cloud fallback. Without a usable PIN Lock — not installed, not verified by the Agent, not answering, unlicensed, without an owner PIN, or locked out — the chat is unavailable, no approval is offered, and the page says to use the SmartBuildOS portal.

      Anyone at the screen sees (chat locked)After an owner PIN (chat unlocked)
      • Status: online, licensed, assistant set up, learning on or off, in one line.
      • Approvals: how many requests are waiting, how many this screen may review and how many need the portal.
      • Whether PIN Lock is ready for this screen, or why not.
      • Works only on the home network.
      • The button Unlock with owner PIN. No question, answer, suggestion or Explain action is sent to a locked page.
      • Three suggested questions (Is everything in the house working?, What happened today?, Does anything need attention?), Explain what just happened, and Your question (up to 500 characters). Each question is answered on its own; there are no follow-ups.
      • The last 10 questions and answers of this screen, kept in memory only and cleared after 15 minutes without use. A touchscreen answer is shown only there: it never reaches AI_LAST_RESPONSE or AI Response Ready.
      • A Lock button. The chat relocks after five minutes without use, on Lock, when the page closes or goes silent for 75 seconds, when the driver restarts, and on every screen at once when PIN Lock stops being available.

      What a touchscreen answer may draw on is set twice: the homeowner's portal switch for household activity (below) and the dealer's Touchscreen Detail property, which can only lower it. With the switch off, answers use equipment status and recent events only.

      Approving one item at the touchscreen with one PIN

      Only when the homeowner has switched Approve at the touchscreen with an owner PIN on in the portal. A person at the wall screen:

      1. Sees how many requests wait in Approvals and presses Review next item.
      2. Enters an owner PIN on the PIN pad (Owner PINs only. The PIN goes to PIN Lock, not to AI Core.). The page posts it to PIN Lock directly; PIN Lock answers only whether an owner code was entered. Guest and vendor codes are always refused, and wrong PINs count against PIN Lock's own lockout.
      3. Sees that one request: its title, description and risk. AI Core holds a proof for that one item for 60 seconds.
      4. Presses Approve or Decline. The proof is used once and deleted, whatever the answer; the outcome (queued, declined, failed, expired, or the reason it was refused) is shown in words.
      5. The next item needs a new PIN. Unlocking the chat never approves anything, and an approval PIN never unlocks the chat.

      The homeowner is notified of every touchscreen approve and decline. SmartBuildOS records "approved at the touchscreen with an owner PIN" and nothing that identifies which code was used: no code name and no slot leave PIN Lock. The platform also checks, in code and by a database CHECK, that the item is low or medium risk; it accepts each verification once (single-use nonce) and only inside the window [now − 120 s, now + 60 s]; and it allows 30 item details and 10 decisions an hour per property. The cloud cannot see the PIN itself: it relies on AI Core's statement that PIN Lock verified an owner PIN, inside those bounds (KI-58). These limits are the conductor's rulings, open for the owner to confirm (owner decisions 16–20).

      What an owner PIN can and cannot approve

      At the touchscreen, with one owner PIN per itemIn the SmartBuildOS portal only
      • Low-risk action proposals: lights, thermostats, scenes.
      • Medium-risk proposals: an action a SmartBuildOS driver declared (Chapter 6), unless that driver controls a lock or security equipment.
      • Locks, garage doors and security, and every action of a driver that controls a lock or security equipment (high risk).
      • Recommendations, concierge bookings and other external actions, programming hand-offs.
      • Learning consent, erase, and every setting, including the two touchscreen switches.

      The homeowner's two switches (portal)

      In the portal, Your home assistant › Approvals › Touchscreen permissions (Your Control4 touchscreen), per property: Both are off until you turn them on. Your integrator can turn them off but never on.

      SwitchOff (the default)On
      Approve at the touchscreen with an owner PINRequests are decided in the portal only.An owner PIN from PIN Lock can approve or decline the assistant's low- and medium-risk requests at the touchscreen, one PIN per item; locks, garage doors, security, recommendations, bookings and settings stay in the portal. The homeowner is notified of every touchscreen decision. Turning it on needs the licence feature AI_ACTIONS.
      Let touchscreen answers use household activityTouchscreen answers use equipment status and recent events only, so a guest at a wall screen cannot ask when the house is usually empty.Touchscreen answers may use the household's activity patterns. Entering a PIN does not change this; only this switch does.

      Only the portal route /api/portal/ai-core/touchscreen can switch either on. Staff see both switches, who changed them and when, and can only switch one off (/api/monitoring/ai-core/touchscreen; asking it to switch one on is refused). In System Studio a touchscreen decision reads Approved at the touchscreen with an owner PIN. Screenshot pending: no screenshot of the switches or of the tile exists from the platform's browser runs, so this guide describes them in words.

      Pre-approved rules and homeowner consent

      In execute_low_risk, a low action runs without a per-action approval only when an active rule covers it exactly: verb SET_LIGHT, SET_THERMOSTAT or ACTIVATE_SCENE only; a device or room scope; numeric bounds inside the queue's clamp; allowed values (thermostat modes); an optional time window with an IANA time zone; an expiry within 365 days.

      1. Staff create it in Studio › Recommendations › Pre-approved rules (POST /api/monitoring/ai-core/rules, needs monitoring:manage and homecontrol:manage): Save rule (inactive until consent) → Saved — inactive until the homeowner consents.
      2. The homeowner consents in the portal (What the assistant may do without asking › Review and allow), which sends { decision: "consent", content_hash }; a hash that is not the stored rule's answers 409 content_mismatch, so the homeowner consents to exactly what they saw.
      3. Either side can revoke at once (Revoke now in the portal; DELETE in Studio). Revocation is final and never needs the licence.

      A rule never covers locks, garage doors or security, and a learned basis never makes anything automatic.

      Programming changes: a hand-off carried by a person

      AI Core never applies programming. A recommendation that needs a programming change becomes a programming hand-off (Studio › Recommendations › Programming hand-offs; /api/monitoring/ai-core/programming), created only from a recommendation in reviewed, approved or implementing. Its states: proposed → accepted (Accept — I will carry this into Composer) → in_composer (needs a Composer project or reference) → completed, or rejected / withdrawn. Moving it to accepted, in Composer or completed needs the person's own Composer Studio edit permission. The page states: AI Core never edits Composer programming, never writes a blueprint and never records a checkpoint. Composer Studio has no per-project programming field, so nothing can be accepted into a blueprint automatically (owner decision 10).

      Safety limitations

      • observe denies every non-read class: the AI may not even ask.
      • Locks, garage doors and security partitions always need explicit homeowner approval per action, are never automatic, and are never proposed on learned behaviour alone. A disarm code is never taken by AI Core; approving sends the action on to the queue's own Control4 approval, a second separate confirmation that collects any code.
      • The homeowner's Composer Remote Control tier on the Agent still bounds what is possible: low verbs need the controller capability comfort_v1 (Comfort) and lock/garage/security need control_v1 (Full control).
      • A medium action (a driver-declared action) is never automatic: no pre-approved rule can match it, learned behaviour alone never proposes it, and the homeowner approves each one.
      • No tool can read a credential: there is no credential risk class.
      • A physical device change from an approved AI action has not been demonstrated: it needs a controller (checklist 7.9).

      AI Workflow Simulator

      AI Workflow Simulator

      Simulation · sample data

      Pick an example and step through what the orchestrator does: the tools offered to that persona (computed live from the per-persona tool lists in orchestrator/server.ts and concierge/server.ts, filtered as orchestrator/turn.ts offeredTools does), the real tool names the model requests, the permission engine's decision for each call (the same transcription the Permissions Explorer uses), approvals, and the evidence-checked answer. Event ids, devices, venues and times are made up; no model was called.

        Chapter 9

        Lifestyle Concierge

        The concierge lets a homeowner plan a restaurant reservation with the assistant and approve every step. As built, the only provider that can complete a request is a labelled SIMULATION sandbox, which staff switch on per property: nothing is ever booked at a real restaurant. Real vendors, calendars and Places discovery are each blocked on something outside engineering, and this chapter says what.

        What exists

        • Eleven concierge tools, offered only in a homeowner's portal conversation and gated by the licence feature AI_CONCIERGE: concierge_list_providers, concierge_list_services, concierge_suggest_reservation, concierge_search_places, concierge_search_availability, concierge_present_options, concierge_submit_booking, concierge_check_booking, concierge_calendar_list, concierge_calendar_add, concierge_offer_scene. Only concierge_submit_booking and concierge_calendar_add are in the external risk class; the rest read, or record something for the homeowner to act on. Approving the search, choosing an option, final confirmation and recovery choices have no tool: they exist only as the homeowner's own portal actions.
        • A request state machine enforced in code and again by a database trigger (below).
        • A provider registry that lists every vendor with its true status, an adapter only for the sandbox, and a database that admits only the sandbox as a provider.
        • Google Calendar and Microsoft Graph adapters with homeowner OAuth (PKCE, encrypted tokens), and Google Places search — built against documented wire shapes and never called live.
        • The portal's Concierge and Calendar areas in Your home assistant, and a read-only staff view with the sandbox switch.

        The request state machine

        Each transition names who may take it (concierge/lifecycle.ts, ai_core_concierge_transition_allowed). Staff, automations and the controller can make no transition.

        FromTo (who)
        suggestedsearch_approved (homeowner), cancelled (homeowner), expired (system)
        search_approvedoptions_presented (model, homeowner), failed (system), cancelled (homeowner), expired (system)
        options_presentedoption_selected (homeowner), search_approved (homeowner), cancelled, expired
        option_selecteddetails_presented (system), options_presented (homeowner), failed (system), cancelled, expired
        details_presentedfinal_confirmed (homeowner, bound to the hash of exactly these details), options_presented (homeowner), cancelled, expired
        final_confirmedsubmitted (homeowner, model), details_presented (system), cancelled, expired
        submittedconfirmed, simulated_confirmed, failed (provider — only its own getBooking)
        confirmed, simulated_confirmedcancelled (homeowner; a real booking is cancelled at the provider first)
        failedsubmitted (homeowner), cancelled (homeowner), expired (system)
        cancelled, expired— (final)

        Step by step, as the homeowner sees it: the assistant (or the homeowner's New reservation request form) records a suggestion; the homeowner approves the search (Search for availability? Nothing is searched until you say yes.); availability is searched and up to 5 options presented (from ≤ 12 candidates); the homeowner picks one; the server builds the exact details; the homeowner gives final confirmation of those details (Please check every line. Only these exact details will be sent.); the request is submitted (idempotent; at most 3 submissions); the provider's own getBooking decides the outcome. A suggestion expires after 48 hours; at most 10 open requests per property. A suggestion based on learned behaviour never goes further than a suggestion without the homeowner.

        The model cannot submit early. concierge_submit_booking takes request_id and details_hash; the engine answers require_approval(homeowner) for the external class, and the tool acts only on the homeowner's recorded final confirmation of exactly that hash. Otherwise it is refused 409 not_confirmed — The homeowner has not given final confirmation for exactly these details. — and the refusal is audited. The AI Workflow Simulator in Chapter 8 shows this.

        The provider registry: who can book

        ProviderStatus in the registryReason it gives
        OpenTablerequires_partner_agreementBooking APIs only for approved integration partners; production use needs partner approval and a formal agreement.
        Yelp Reservationsrequires_partner_agreementReserved for Yelp partners and disabled by default.
        SevenRoomsrequires_partner_agreementAPI access provisioned through a partnership, per venue.
        Resyno_sanctioned_apiNo public booking API; enforces against unsanctioned bots and autonomous agents.
        Tockno_sanctioned_apiPublic documentation describes the data model only; no booking-write API.
        Reserve with Googlenot_applicableLets booking providers list inventory on Google; no API to book on a diner's behalf.
        simulatedA simulated inventory for demonstration and testing. Nothing is ever booked at a real restaurant. Off unless your integrator enables it for this home.

        No adapter exists for any real vendor, no tool takes a provider name, and the server — never the model — chooses the provider: the first usable one, which today is the sandbox when staff enabled it, else none (No reservation provider is connected for this home…). Scraping or driving consumer booking sites is prohibited regardless. Writing a real adapter needs a signed vendor agreement, the vendor's public API documentation and a migration (the database CHECK admits only sandbox).

        The SIMULATION sandbox

        • Staff switch it on per property (PATCH /api/monitoring/ai-core/concierge { sandbox_enabled }, needs monitoring:manage and homecontrol:manage). Off by default.
        • Every venue name, option id, booking reference and confirmation reference begins with SIMULATION / SIM-; every object carries simulated: true; the portal marks each card, button and dialog SIMULATION (Confirm the SIMULATION — nothing real is booked).
        • Its bookings are recorded simulated_confirmed, never confirmed (the database refuses confirmed for a simulated request) and are never added to a calendar (simulated_booking).
        • Deterministic: availability depends only on venue, date, time and party size (party ≤ 8). One venue, SIMULATION — Full House Grill (sandbox; always sold out at booking), always fails at submission so the recovery path can be shown.

        Approvals and the portal actions

        The homeowner's steps are actions on POST /api/portal/ai-core/concierge (30 a minute): create {criteria} (suggests and approves the search in one step), approve_search, search, select_option, back_to_options, search_again, confirm {details_hash, submit?}, submit, check, recover, cancel, add_to_calendar, answer_scene_offer. Criteria: party size 1–20, a date within 180 days, a time window, an IANA time zone, optional cuisine, area and a note that is not sent to the restaurant. The licence is not needed for the safe direction: cancel, declining a scene offer, and stopping a failed request. Staff have a read-only view and cannot move a request.

        Confirmation

        Only the provider's own answer can make a request confirmed. A submission is never assumed: a created booking is verified with getBooking before it is settled; a timeout or unknown error is resolved by asking the provider; while it is unanswered the card reads Sent … not yet confirmed with Check with the provider. A sandbox request settles as simulated_confirmed with a SIMULATION reference (not a real confirmation).

        Failed-booking recovery

        A failed request waits for the homeowner, who chooses among the recovery options the failure allows (concierge/service.ts recoveryFor):

        FailureChoices
        rate limited, timeout, unknown, unavailableTry sending it again (retry), Look for other options (alternatives), Stop this request (stop)
        sold out, not confirmed, validationalternatives, stop

        Retry submits the same confirmed details again (at most 3 submissions). Alternatives stops the failed request and starts a new one with the same criteria, its search already approved. Stop cancels it. The homeowner is notified (Reservation not made).

        Calendar and Places

        The homeowner connects Google Calendar or an Outlook (Microsoft) calendar in the portal's Calendar area (/api/portal/ai-core/calendar, connect and callback per provider). Connecting lets the concierge add an event only when you say yes to that specific event. Reading your calendar is a separate yes. Reading is a separate switch (Let the assistant read my calendar); writing is only ever an offer (concierge_calendar_add) that the homeowner confirms (Yes, add this one event), and only for a booking the provider confirmed. Disconnecting deletes the stored tokens; events already added stay. Google Places search (concierge_search_places) finds restaurants only; it cannot book.

        Microsoft calendarAI_CORE_CALENDAR_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID, AI_CORE_CALENDAR_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET, AI_CORE_CALENDAR_MICROSOFT_TENANT (default common)not configured

        Chapter 10

        System Studio — Intelligence

        Staff see and manage AI Core in System Studio, on the property's Intelligence destination: six pages, each with its own tabs. Every page reads stored records; only AI Conversations runs a model (the connectivity test on Provider & settings only lists the provider's models). This chapter says what each page shows and what it honestly cannot. Screens are fixture-mode screenshots with sample data.

        Navigation and permissions

        Intelligence is a ninth top-level destination (section id intelligence; the owner decided on 18 November 2026 that it stays one, checklist 8.10), shown only where the property's controller holds the SBOS_AI_CORE entitlement (Studio capability ai-core). Studio permissions: intelligence.view (from monitoring:view), intelligence.manage (monitoring:manage), intelligence.raise-mode (monitoring:manage and homecontrol:manage); household pages need household.view (homecontrol:view). Every page shows a fixture banner in fixture mode, a Sample data mark, and states for not entitled, permission denied, empty and error.

        Page (section id)TabsNeedsRoutes
        Intelligence — AI Overview (intelligence, alias ai-overview)Overview · Provider & settingsintelligence.viewoverview, settings, credentials, credentials/test, usage
        Household Usage (ai-usage)Overview · Rooms · Lighting · Scenes · Entertainment · Climate · Shades · Automation · Trendshousehold.viewhousehold-usage
        Flight Recorder Intelligence (ai-flight-recorder)search, incident viewintelligence.viewflight-recorder?view=search|incident
        Recommendations (ai-recommendations)Recommendations · Programming hand-offs · Actions & approvals · Pre-approved rules · Pending memorieshousehold.view; AI_LEARNING, AI_ACTIONSrecommendations, programming, actions, rules, memories
        Service (ai-service)Recurring problems · Predictive maintenance · Driver health · Network correlationintelligence.viewservice/findings, driver-health, playbook, ticket
        Conversations (ai-conversations)thread list, conversationintelligence.view; asking needs monitoring:manageconversations, conversations/[id]/messages (SSE)
        Connected drivers (ai-drivers; staff only)one listintelligence.view; events and state need household.viewdrivers

        Routes are under /api/monitoring/ai-core/. A read-only staff concierge route (concierge, with the sandbox switch) exists without a page of its own.

        AI Overview

        Cards for the AI connection (driver registered, version, last seen, protocol, Agent link), the AI provider (models, masked key and test state, fallback, permission mode, learning), AI health (last provider call, spend and requests against limits), the System health score as System Intelligence last wrote it, Monitored devices worded “reported offline” / “not reported offline” / status unknown, Learning (patterns, last analysis, recommendations, active investigations, jobs), Recent events with clock-suspect marks, and AI usage this month with known spend kept apart from requests whose cost is unknown.

        What it cannot show: a health score System Intelligence never computed (AI Core does not invent a score of its own); a verified online state (“not reported offline” is not online); learned data without Home control view and the AI_LEARNING feature; the true bill when some costs are unknown (the known total is a floor).

        Provider & settings

        The second tab of the Intelligence page: provider keys, the AI Core settings, limits, permission mode, learning and exclusions, with a revision and a 409 on a conflicting save. Described in full in Chapter 3; the month-to-date usage behind it is GET /api/monitoring/ai-core/usage (UTC month; unknown-cost requests counted separately, never as zero).

        Household Usage

        Usage Analytics daily figures, recorded interactions (Counted from recorded interactions and state changes. Not occupancy, not people.), measured occupancy kept apart (Only where an occupancy or motion sensor was the source.), and learned patterns by room, lighting, scenes, entertainment, climate, shades, automation and trends, with each detector's last status including insufficient_history.

        What it cannot show: climate and shade usage counts (No usage aggregate exists for climate…, …for shades: nothing counts shade movements per day.); people; occupancy from device interactions; a trend for a 1-day range.

        Flight Recorder Intelligence

        Runs the deterministic read tools server-side — flight_recorder_search_events, devices_list, flight_recorder_analyze_incident, flight_recorder_correlate_events — with no model and no write. Search by time, text, type, severity, device and room; open an event for its incident view: What came before it, ranked (Ranked by strength of evidence, then closeness. Confirmed rests on a shared trace id; possible is a lead from timing, device or room — not a finding.) and a device correlation timeline. The hypotheses (part of the same traced sequence; a command sent shortly before; a device offline before it; a restart; a cloud-connection change; a programming marker; a project change; something else in the same room), each confirmed only by a shared trace id. Explain with AI seeds a conversation with the selected events: a bounded question plus validated event ids, offered to the model only as references to look up — the evidence check still accepts only ids a tool returned in that turn (nothing is sent until Ask is pressed). Household modules are excluded without homecontrol:view; a bad filter answers 422 invalid_filter.

        What it cannot show: a cause where nothing recorded points to one (…that is not proof there was none); events older than retention; a trustworthy time for clock-suspect events. A What is missing or unreliable in these results panel lists gaps, retention edges and suspect clocks.

        Recommendations, actions, rules, hand-offs and pending memories

        • Recommendations — Found by deterministic detectors over stored events. Recommendations never run anything. Filter by kind, status, confidence and customer visibility; each shows its approver (the integrator or the homeowner), confidence, whether it needs a programming change and whether the homeowner can see it; the detail lists its evidence with Open in Flight Recorder Intelligence. Staff mark reviewed, record the integrator's approval, dismiss, or toggle visibility (monitoring:manage). A recommendation needing both parties (no detector produces one today) is approved only when the integrator and the homeowner have each approved it, and the page shows whose approval is awaited; staff can never approve on the homeowner's behalf. Evidence references are labelled with the store each points into: Flight Recorder rows link to Flight Recorder Intelligence, service evidence is labelled and never linked.
        • Programming hand-offs — Chapter 8.
        • Actions & approvals — every AI-proposed action with its basis (Asked for explicitly, From a recommendation, Learned pattern), engine decision and required approver. Staff approve or decline only low actions a person asked for (homecontrol:manage); a lock, garage or security action reads Awaiting the homeowner…, and after the homeowner's approval Queued — awaiting the homeowner's approval in Control4. Staff cannot approve it.
        • Pre-approved rules — create and revoke rules; each is Saved — inactive until the homeowner consents (Chapter 8).
        • Pending memories — Memories the AI model suggested during conversations. None is used for anything until a person accepts it. Accept or reject (needs Monitoring manage and Home control view).

        What it cannot show: evidence no longer held (None of the referenced events is still in Flight Recorder history…). The homeowner's half of an approval happens in the portal's Recommendations area, not here.

        AI Service Intelligence

        Computed from stored monitoring data by fixed rules. The AI does not invent these findings; it can only explain them in a conversation. Four tabs: Recurring problems (recurring device failures and incidents, with evidence, a generic troubleshooting playbook and the network around the finding), Predictive maintenance (rising failure trends, counts in past windows), Driver health (SmartBuildOS modules' own state) and Network correlation (UniFi alerts linked as confirmed same hardware or only possible). A service ticket is drafted from a finding and created only when a staff member with tickets:create confirms it (one open ticket per finding); the AI tool service_draft_ticket only drafts.

        What it cannot show (the page lists it): the cause of a device going offline (the platform records that it went offline, not why); health of a driver that has not reported (shown as “not reported”, never healthy or unhealthy); third-party drivers' internal errors; a network cause without network data; a forecast (trends are counts in past windows).

        AI Conversations

        Questions are answered from stored evidence. Every historical claim cites events a tool returned in the same turn; anything else is removed. A thread list per system; a conversation shows each answer split into Confirmed (each rests on a stored event a tool returned and a confirmed link), Possible (Leads from timing, device or room — not findings.), Unknown and Suggested next steps, every cited event clickable into Flight Recorder Intelligence. How this answer was produced streams the turn live (Server-Sent Events): tools offered, each tool requested by its real name, the engine's decision, the evidence check. Asking needs monitoring:manage (a turn spends the property's AI budget); without homecontrol:view Household tools are not offered to you.

        What it cannot show: a real model answer — no provider key exists, so a real turn ends AI Core has no AI provider key for this property. Add one in System Studio.; token streaming (the answer arrives whole); an answer without evidence (replaced by I don't have evidence for that.).

        Connected drivers

        Staff only; the homeowner portal has no counterpart (homeowners see only the approval items). It lists every SmartBuildOS driver instance of the property's system: the drivers that report to AI Core joined with the Agent's module registry (Chapter 6). For each one it shows whether the Agent verified it (Verified by the Agent, or a warning that The SmartBuildOS Agent could not verify that this module is the driver it claims to be, whose reports are labelled unverified and whose declared actions cannot be proposed), drivers that registered but never reported, dropped reports, what the driver described, its Declared read-only queries and Declared actions (proposal only; the homeowner approves each) with their effective risk, its latest state, recent diagnostics and recent events. A driver that controls a lock or security equipment says that every action it declares is high risk, for the homeowner in the portal only, never with a touchscreen PIN. Driver text is shown as text; nothing on the page runs anything. Events and state are household activity: they need Home control view as well. Route: GET /api/monitoring/ai-core/drivers.

        Tested by the platform worker: unit tests and a browser walk in fixture mode (checklist 12.12, worker-reported); not deployed. Screenshot pending: no capture of this page from the platform's browser runs exists, so it is described in words.

        Chapter 11

        Control4 Programming

        Everything AI Core exposes to Composer: 11 commands, 4 actions, 23 properties, 10 events, 11 variables and 5 conditionals. The tables below are generated from the same data the Command Reference uses, which a test compares name for name with driver.xml.

        Commands and programming parameters

        Parameters arrive as strings. Every value is validated; typed text over its limit is refused, not cut. Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points), as the platform counts them. A refused command sends nothing and sets Last Error, AI_LAST_ERROR and AI Status (refused locally (<code>)). At most 10 commands a minute; the 11th is refused rate_limited. ROOM is a room name or id (a STRING, not a room selector), resolved against the devices in the project; a typed ROOM longer than 64 characters is refused (… (use the room id)). LIST labels normalise to codes (Last 7 Days → last_7_days); an empty optional LIST takes its default, an empty required one is refused <PARAM>: is required. A command whose room (or whose device's room) is excluded in System Studio is refused not_permitted, except AI_ASK and AI_SEND_NOTIFICATION (the cloud decides those).

        RequiredOptional, with default
        QUESTION (AI_ASK); ROOM (AI_ANALYZE_ROOM, AI_SUGGEST_SCENE); NAME (AI_RECORD_EVENT); KEY, VALUE (AI_SET_CONTEXT); STATEMENT (AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE); OCCASION; TYPE and PERIOD (AI_GENERATE_REPORT — no defaults); exactly one of DEVICE / ROOM (AI_START_DIAGNOSTIC; DEVICE 0, Composer's empty selector, counts as none); TITLE, MESSAGE (AI_SEND_NOTIFICATION)CATEGORY → General (AI_RECORD_EVENT); AUDIENCE → Homeowner (AI_SEND_NOTIFICATION); ROOM (AI_ASK, AI_RECORD_EVENT, AI_LEARN_PREFERENCE) and DETAIL (AI_RECORD_EVENT) → none

        Text sent to the cloud

        The platform refuses the whole request (invalid_args) for one text field over its bound, or containing a character of its UNPRINTABLE set (U+0000–U+0008, U+000B–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F, U+2028, U+2029). So every text field is cleaned before it is sent (aicore.commands.sanitise): every C0 control (TAB and LF too), DEL, every C1 control, U+2028 and U+2029 becomes a space; a byte that is not well-formed UTF-8 is dropped; the ends are trimmed with the platform's whitespace set. Names Director supplies are then cut on a character boundary to the platform's bound — room_name 64, device_name 120 characters — and a name with nothing printable left is not sent. Typed text (QUESTION, STATEMENT, VALUE, OCCASION, TITLE, MESSAGE, NAME, DETAIL) is cleaned the same way and refused over its bound.

        The cloud body carries typed text whole; only the envelope's copy is bounded. Every payload string is cut to 512 bytes and every label to 120 bytes, between two UTF-8 characters, before the shared envelope sees it (the cut marks the envelope partial): an AI_ASK question of 500 three-byte characters is 1,500 bytes. The shared envelope library used by the other SmartBuildOS drivers still cuts at a byte and can split a character (KNOWN-ISSUES KI-1, open).

        AI_RECORD_EVENT is a marker, not learning

        AI_RECORD_EVENT (NAME ≤ 120, DETAIL ≤ 400, ROOM, CATEGORY) makes no cloud call: it records an ai_core.record envelope on the durable event path (severity warning for Security and Safety). It is a dealer's explicit marker (architect's ruling, 18 November 2026): it is recorded whether learning is off, on or paused, but it still honours the exclusions — refused for an excluded room (… is excluded by the AI Core configuration) or category (not recorded (excluded_category)). The cloud's learning engine never learns from it.

        AI_SET_CONTEXT

        The context key is sent as key in the set_context cloud body (the platform validates key) and as context_key in the ai_core.command envelope, because the envelope's credential rules redact a field named key. The platform keeps one value per system and key and answers completed at once.

        What happens after a cloud command

        Validate → new request_id (aic-<uuid>, written to AI_LAST_REQUEST_ID) → ai_core.command envelope (correlation id = request id) → cloud request with idempotency_key = request id → the Agent POSTs the platform route. Body: {command, request_id, <normalised args>} plus room_id/room_name or device_id/device_name; the body names are the platform's (rpc/ops.ts OP_BODIES, which refuses the whole request for an unknown key). Sync Now's status body is {request_id} only — status takes no field of its own. The platform answers at once:

        AnswerMeaningShown
        status=ok, result.accepted=true with a job_idaccepted as a job; it waits for deliver_result (≤ 20, 30 min)AI Status Working: N request(s) waiting for a result; AI_STATUS working
        status=ok, result.accepted=true, no job_idcompleted now (set_context, send_notification, learn_preference); nothing is delivered later and AI Response Ready is not firedAI Status stays Ready; counter cloud_completed
        status=ok without accepted=truenot success (cloud_refused)Last Error …answered without accepting…
        not_permitted, invalid_args, unsupported, payload_too_large, agent_not_paired, cloud_refused, otherrefused, not retriedLast Error refused by SmartBuildOS: <code>; AI Status — last request refused (<code>)
        rate_limited (the platform's per-system limits on send_notification and test_provider, or the Agent's bucket; after 2 retries, same key)refused: an answer, not silenceLast Error rate limited by SmartBuildOS (rate_limited); try again later
        cloud_unreachable, deadline_exceeded, target_unavailable (after 2 retries, same key)not deliveredLast Error no answer from SmartBuildOS (<code>)
        incompatible_protocolv1 Agentrefused locally before sending

        Actions (Composer Actions tab)

        Properties

        All read-only except Log Level and Log Mode.

        Events

        Event ids are permanent (programming binds by id). Events 1–8 and 10 are fired by the platform through deliver_result / raise_event; event 9 only by the driver itself.

        Wire the events you care about to the Notification Agent for push or email: a driver cannot send push or email itself.

        Variables

        Ids 4000–4010, order frozen. AI_LAST_CORRELATION_ID (4010) is an addition beyond the brief's ten: it holds the correlation_id of the last raise_event — for Approval Required, Action Completed and Action Failed, the platform's action id — so programming and support can tie the event to the action in System Studio. An event without one sets it to empty, so it never names an earlier event's subject. Sizes are in bytes: AI_LAST_RESPONSE ≤ 1024 (a longer result keeps its first ≤ 1021 bytes, cut between two UTF-8 characters, followed by ...), AI_LAST_EVENT_DETAIL ≤ 512, Last Error / AI_LAST_ERROR ≤ 240. LEARNING_ACTIVE is false until a valid configuration or set_learning switches learning on. All except AI_STATUS, AGENT_CONNECTED and LEARNING_ACTIVE (recomputed at start) are persisted and repainted after a reload. AI_STATUS shows starting until the first state is computed.

        Chapter 12

        Security

        The controller stays light and holds no secrets; the cloud authorizes every tool call with deterministic code; household activity is a second gate; and the homeowner keeps control of what is learned.

        Credential storage

        • Provider keys are customer-supplied and entered only in System Studio (Provider & settings). They are stored as secret-box ciphertext in ai_core_provider_credentials; the key field is write-only and every answer carries only provider, scope, ••••last4 and test status (the PUT answer is cache-control: no-store). Key changes are audited (credential.stored, credential.rotated, credential.store_refused, credential.deleted, credential.tested).
        • Keys never transit the controller. The driver refuses any configuration document containing a credential-shaped key or a display string that looks like a key.
        • The provider layer removes key material from every string that leaves it; connectivity tests return an error kind, never the vendor message.
        • The Agent's pairing token authenticates its cloud calls; module tokens never leave the controller.
        • No AI tool can read a secret: the credential risk class has no tool and is refused by the engine.
        • Calendar OAuth tokens are stored encrypted (ai_core_concierge_connections), the OAuth state as a hash with an encrypted PKCE verifier; no route ever returns a token.

        Permissions

        The permission engine (src/lib/ai-core/authz/engine.ts) is pure, synchronous and total: every input it does not recognise is a denial. Its inputs are built by the server from the session — actor, property permission mode, tool (risk, household flag, verb, feature), target (device type from the registry), controller capabilities, entitlement features, pre-approved rules, learning basis and the route gate's would-deny flag.

        Risk classExamplesRule
        readhistory, registry, usageallowed in every mode, subject to role and household gate
        lowlights, thermostat within bounds, scenesobserve: deny · recommend: approval · execute_low_risk: allow only on a matching pre-approved rule, else approval
        highlocks, garage, security, access controlobserve: deny · otherwise explicit homeowner approval per action; never on learned behaviour
        externalreservations, purchases, calendar writesobserve: deny · otherwise explicit homeowner confirmation; never for an automation or on learned behaviour
        programmingpersistent programmingnever executed; a recommendation only
        credentialreading secretsno tool exists; refused

        Permissions Explorer

        Faithful transcription of authz/engine.ts

        Choose who is asking, the property's mode and an operation. The decision below is computed by a line-for-line JavaScript transcription of authorizeToolCall, ruleMatches and targetClassOf from the platform repo; the automated test checks it against the real TypeScript engine across the whole matrix.

        Actor
        Licence features
        Controller capabilities (Composer Remote Control tier)
        Matrix: every mode × operation for this actor and basis

        The explorer below is checked against the engine as it is at platform commit 2ebbd5bd2: observe denies every non-read class (observe_mode_no_actions); a learned basis (anything that is not explicit_request, recommendation or preapproved_rule) is never enough for a medium, high or external action (learned_behaviour_insufficient); a medium action (a driver-declared action) always needs the homeowner and no pre-approved rule is consulted (medium_risk_needs_homeowner) and makes a low action need the homeowner; an automation may never take an external action; a staff-only tool (the service tools) is denied to a homeowner or an automation and a homeowner-only tool (concierge) to staff or an automation (audience_not_permitted); risk is only ever escalated by the target class, never lowered.

        Property isolation

        • Tenant and property come from the session or the Agent's pairing token only; the controller route never reads them from a frame body.
        • All AI Core tables (ai_core_*) carry a composite foreign key to the property, have row-level security on, and grant access only to the service role (revoke-first).
        • Device ids are validated against the property's registry; a homeowner can act only on their own client's properties; own-scope staff roles see only their clients' properties (anything else is 404).
        • Idempotency keys are unique; replays are refused; per-property rate limits live in the database.
        • Cross-property and cross-tenant isolation tests pass in simulation (7.5).

        Route gates

        Every staff route checks, in order: the platform permission (monitoring:view or manage); the audit-mode would-deny flag; a uuid property_id in the caller's company (another company's looks like no property: 404); a linked Control4 system; the SBOS_AI_CORE entitlement (403 not_entitled, 503 when unreadable). Families add the household grant (homecontrol:view), homecontrol:manage for action writes, the AI_LEARNING / AI_ACTIONS / AI_CONCIERGE feature, and for conversations a property visible to the caller's own session. Portal routes resolve the client portal session, the property (must belong to the caller's client), the system, and the licence only for the directions that need it: the homeowner's learning controls and every "safe direction" (decline, revoke, cancel, dismiss, disconnect) never need the licence.

        Six operations staff cannot send

        Through the staff route POST /api/monitoring/control4/commands, staff may send refresh_status and run_diagnostic to AI Core; deliver_result, raise_event, set_learning, apply_config, invoke_driver_action and run_driver_query are refused with 403. Each is produced only from a record the platform owns (a job's result, an action, the settings, a homeowner-approved driver action, a query a tool asked for), so a hand-made copy cannot fake an answer or an approval event, switch learning on over a homeowner's pause, or run a house action nobody approved.

        Approval policies

        See Chapter 8. In short: low actions — the requester (or the homeowner for automations and learned behaviour), unless a consented rule covers them in execute_low_risk; medium, high and external — the homeowner, per action; programming — a person in Composer Studio. The homeowner may approve low and medium proposals at the touchscreen with one owner PIN per item when they have switched that on in the portal (Chapter 8); everything else is approved in the portal.

        Audit

        ai_core_audit_events is append-only (a trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE except a foreign key nulling its pointer). The orchestrator writes turn.started, provider.call, budget.refused, turn.round_limit and answer.invalid; every tool call records its decision; credential changes are recorded (e.g. credential.deleted). The audit trail for every tool call and decision is Completed in simulation (7.7).

        Privacy controls and prompt-injection defence

        • Learning is off by default; household activity needs homecontrol:view in addition to the route gate; the homeowner can pause, exclude, correct, export and erase what was learned, and a pause reaches the controller and the cloud at once (Chapter 7).
        • No retention job exists for any ai_core_* table: rows stay until a route, a cascade or a company deletion removes them.
        • The system prompt is a static constant that contains no tenant data; telemetry reaches the model only inside tool results marked {"untrusted":true,"source":…,"data":…}.
        • The tool list is fixed before the first round and does not change because of anything a tool returns. A call the model was talked into by injected text is refused by the engine like any other. Prompt-injection tests with hostile device names, titles and calendar text pass in simulation (7.6).
        • A historical answer with no surviving evidence is replaced in full by I don't have evidence for that.
        • OpenAI calls use store:false.

        Protocol frames

        v1 frames (registration, status, events, command delivery, configuration) and v2 frames (discovery, pub/sub, requests, cloud relay). "auth" = module_id, instance_id, token.

        Event schemas (envelope v1)

        The server adds received_at and clock_suspect. Within one module instance, (boot_id, sequence) orders events; across modules, received_at. Nothing claims a global order.

        AI Core's manifest is { "driver": "sbos.ai_core", "protocol": 2, "capabilities": [] } in substance: it consumes, it serves nothing to other modules.

        Tool definitions

        The 37 tools the platform registry defines, dumped from the registry code (src/dump-tools.mjs; the consistency test compares this list with the live registry). Wire names are what the model sees; ids are internal. Every schema is a closed object. recommendations.create and actions.propose, listed in the architecture, do not exist as such: recommendations come from the deterministic detectors, and actions are one tool per queue verb, plus drivers_propose_action for an action a driver declared (risk medium: it only creates a proposal a person must approve). The model has no notification tool: notifications.send was removed (platform commit c79f42d09) because, being low risk with no verb and no proposal, it could never be allowed; notices come only from the platform's own services (and Composer's AI_SEND_NOTIFICATION).

        Which tools each persona is offered

        A turn is offered every tool in its registry that the permission engine would not outright deny for that actor, audience, mode, licence, household grant and gate (a require_approval tool is offered: calling it records a proposal); a controller job is offered read tools only (orchestrator/turn.ts offeredTools). The registries are composed in orchestrator/server.ts aiCoreRegistry and concierge/server.ts portalConversationDeps:

        Homeowner conversation (portal)homeownerthe same, plus the 11 concierge toolsthe three service tools are staff-only (audience: "staff"): the engine denies them to a homeowner (audience_not_permitted), so they are not offered, and a call by name is refused before the handler runs (the handler’s own refusal, Service intelligence tools are for technicians., stays as a second line). The concierge tools are homeowner-only

        API examples

        Controller route (Agent → platform)

        POST {API URL}/api/integrations/control4/modules/rpc
Authorization: Bearer <Agent pairing token>

{ "module_id": "ai_core", "instance_id": "412", "op": "ask",
  "request_id": "aic-3f1c…", "idempotency_key": "aic-3f1c…",
  "body": { "command": "AI_ASK", "request_id": "aic-3f1c…",
            "question": "Why did the living room lights turn on at 2 AM?",
            "room_id": 12, "room_name": "Living Room" } }

200 { "ok": true,  "result": { "accepted": true, "job_id": "…" } }
200 { "ok": false, "error_code": "unsupported" }      ← business refusal
401                                                  ← token is not a live pairing

        The route answers HTTP 200 for every business outcome. A non-2xx answer goes through the Agent's failure path (Connection Status repaint, Composer event Sync Failed on the Agent). A 2xx ok:false code passes through only if it is one of not_permitted, invalid_args, unsupported, payload_too_large, rate_limited, agent_not_paired; otherwise the module sees cloud_refused. HTTP 429 → rate_limited; other 4xx → cloud_refused; 5xx, transport failure or timeout → cloud_unreachable.

200 { "ok": true, "settings": { … }, "driver_config": { … } }

        Extension guidelines

        1. Extend, do not fork. Use the module contract, command queue, Flight Recorder store, licensing, notifications, audit and secret box that exist.
        2. New tool: defineTool with a dotted lower-case id, a wire name matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$, a declared risk (read, low, high, external, programming), a declared household flag, a closed object schema (additionalProperties: false), and — for any action tool — a resolveTarget that reads the target from the registry. There is no way to declare a credential risk.
        3. New cloud op or capability: add it to the Agent policy table and protocol.ts together; it is a driver release.
        4. New Composer event: append an id (ids are permanent) and add its key to raise_event's closed list on both sides.
        5. Evidence: any historical claim must cite event ids a tool returned in the same turn.
        6. Prove guards: a thing is tested only when a test that fails without it passes.
        7. Label simulations as simulations in code, UI, tests and docs.

                The migrations: independent review

                There are twelve AI Core migration files: 20261118120000, 120100, 140000, 150000, 160000, 170000, 180000, 190000, 200000, 210000, 211000 and 20261118220000 (the price). Each has a rollback, each is a single transaction with a 5-second lock limit, and the order is enforced both ways. An independent reviewer, a separate worker that wrote none of them, ran two passes on a local database; the second pass found them “ready with conditions” with every first-pass finding closed. One new medium finding remained: on Supabase, creating a policy takes a lock on the sign-in and Storage tables until the file commits. A final lock-ordering fix was in progress when this guide was built. These runs are reviewer-reported; the conductor has not rerun them.

                The reviewer's conditions for applying them:

                1. Files 1–11, then deploy the new app, then file 12. With today's production app, file 12 would make the $150 dealer price public.
                2. Run the pre-flight script first and clear every stop it reports.
                3. Back up the Flight Recorder history before file 9: its first nightly run deletes the whole backlog beyond the windows (30 days events, 90 days traces) in one pass.
                4. Use a quiet window.
                5. Record the versions under their file stamps.

                The review also found database permissions that predate these migrations and that they do not change: the signed-out and ordinary signed-in roles hold TRUNCATE on companies and profiles, and TRIGGER, MAINTAIN and REFERENCES on ai_usage_events (the migrations revoke only TRUNCATE there). That is open for the owner (decision 24). Nothing is applied to any remote database.
